# Document-Driven Information Requests Completion Evidence

## Purpose

This companion file stores historical completion results, test evidence, implementation decisions,
risks, blockers, and older handoff details for the active plan at
`plans/DOCUMENT-DRIVEN-INFORMATION-REQUESTS-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md`.

The active plan stays lean: original plan context, current status, what is next, subsequent planned
work, and the latest implementation result. This file is the durable proof trail.

## Update Protocol

Add detailed implementation evidence newest first under `## Implementation Journal`. When the active
plan's latest implementation result is replaced, ensure the displaced result exists here. Keep exact
commands and outcomes, failed or skipped validations, help documentation review, migrations, changed
files, decisions, assumptions, risks, blockers, and files for the next agent.

## Archived Status Evidence

The following status narrative was moved out of the active plan on 2026-09-03 when the completion
evidence split was created. It is preserved so prior phase completion context remains available
without making the active plan carry every historical implementation phase.

also requires this deployment to have named the same owner in its rollout configuration. Nothing is

enforcement mode. Audit capture, ledger streams, projections, exports, and retention policy lookup

and released. `P2-T2` is complete and allocated V85. A subject is now an opaque organization- or
person-owned identity with a generic subject kind; optional external aliases carry explicit
authorization provenance and remain separate from the primary identity; and merge or supersession
lineage is tenant-bound, single-successor, cycle-safe, and append-only. `P2-T3` is complete and
allocated V86. Reusable request configuration now persists as a stable owner-held Template
Definition, an immutable published Template Version of that definition, the ordered sections of one
Version, the stable requirement identities of the definition, and the bindings that place one
requirement into one Version. A key belongs to one owner across the platform, organization, and
personal key spaces; a version number belongs to one definition; a binding cannot reach a section
outside its own Version or a requirement outside its own definition; a stable requirement key is
never rewritten; and a published Version and everything it holds stop changing except to record
retirement. `P2-T4` is complete and allocated V87. A requirement now says what kind of thing it asks
for, as part of the identity that can never be rewritten, and a Version now says under what policy
it asks: the wording used, who is nominated to answer, whether an answer is owed and what decides
that, which of the platform dispositions may resolve it, whether a reviewer must look at the result,
which confidentiality compartment it falls into, and which repeated occurrence it is answered
against. Permitted answers and supporting evidence are sets keyed to the binding and frozen with the
Version; supporting evidence runs one way, from a requirement that is not a document to a requested
document, so no cycle is reachable; and publishing a Version that asks for typed data now requires
the Schema Version it resolves against. `P2-T5` is complete and allocated V88. A requested document
now states the policy the files answering it are judged by: how many files, how large in total and
individually, how many pages, which content types, what has to be stated about each file out of
issuer, jurisdiction, language, issue date, expiry date, coverage period, certification, and
signature, and which values of the stated ones are accepted. Bounds measured against those dates,
the freshness of the issue date, the validity remaining past the expiry date, and the span and
continuity of the covered period, are admitted only while the date they count from is required.
Waiver and technical conformance are stated as policy rather than assumed. Only a requested document
carries one, alternatives that may be supplied instead are a flat set that cannot be chained in
either direction, and a Version that asks for a document cannot freeze without the policy, without a
capturable basis for every restriction it states, or with a waiver rule and a permitted waived
answer that contradict each other. `P2-T6` is complete and allocated V89. A Version now states which
runtime capabilities the configuration it froze needs somebody to supply, and at which contract
version of each. The set is not an author's claim: it is derived from what the Version actually
configures, and publication refuses a recorded set that disagrees with the derivation in either
direction, so a Version can neither be issued into a runtime that cannot serve it nor be refused for
a capability nothing configured. Whether those contract versions are installed is a separate
question, answered in code where the installed executors are known and asked when a request is
created rather than when the Version freezes: configuration outlives any one deployment, so a
Version stays publishable while the runtime it needs is still being built. An installed executor
serves a range of contract versions, so raising a contract version does not strand what was already
published against the older one, and an installation that cannot say which executor serves a
capability fails startup instead of being narrowed. No executor exists yet, so nothing is served and
every Version that requires anything is refused at issuance. `P2-T7` names five lifecycle operations
over eight configuration tables and needs authorization, entitlement, audit, and read contracts
before the first of them can run, so it is now `P2-T7a` through `P2-T7c`: authoring a draft,
freezing one, and the lifecycle after a Version has frozen. `P2-T7a` is complete and needed no
migration. An owner that passes both gates can now create a Template identity together with the one
Version an author can edit, replace everything that Version configures as a single authored document,
and read the whole thing back through dedicated mappers. Positions are never authored, so a stored
configuration cannot contain a gap or two orders for one thing; a rewrite leaves exactly the second
document behind while the stable requirement identities it stops naming survive for a later Version;
and a requirement cannot change what kind of thing it asks for. Configuration cannot reach a Version
that has stopped being a draft. Who may act is a role and Share decision about the stored owner
rather than about whichever organization the caller has selected, a person authoring for themselves
is a resolvable owner whose changes file under their own audit ownership, and the platform is refused
as a Template owner because it holds neither of the two gates that keep the capability closed.
Template configuration mutations are now a classified audit category of their own, so the catalog
version is 17. A draft Version that configures at least one Requirement can now publish by asking
the database to derive the exact runtime capabilities its stored configuration needs, recording
each at the current contract version, and freezing the Version and Definition in one transaction.
The capability rows are flushed before the Version status changes because the publication trigger
compares them with the same derivation function and the configuration guard freezes them after the
transition. A row lock shared with configuration replacement serializes saving against publication,
an empty draft is refused, and any stored completeness refusal rolls the capability rows and both
status changes back together. `P2-T7c` is complete and needed no migration. An authorized owner can
retire a published Version without removing its configuration, start one new editable Version from
an explicitly selected published source, and clone a selected published Version into a new
owner-scoped Definition and draft. Both copy operations reconstruct the authored document into new
rows and omit the source capability rows, so publication derives the new Version's requirements
again. New-Version attempts lock the Definition before checking for an existing draft or allocating
the next number, and cloning locks the source Definition after read authorization so retirement
cannot race the copy. Retirement and new-Version creation have classified audit events, and the
catalog version is 18. `P2-T8` is complete and needed no migration. Every Template service operation
is now reachable over HTTP through one thin adapter at `/information-request-templates`, and the
first-party client calls it through a typed service module. The adapter parses only path, query, and
body shape, delegates every owner, entitlement, lifecycle, and persistence decision, and maps
refusals to stable statuses: configuration validation to `400`, a state that forbids the operation
to `409`, an unknown Template to `404`, an owner refusal to `403`, and an unauthenticated caller to

retirement, new-Version creation, and cloning are each a `POST` to their own path and each names an
exact source Version instead of resolving whatever is latest. Template administration is not in the
authentication filter's exclusion list, which a test now pins, so it stays behind access-token
verification. `P2-T9` is complete and allocated V90. An existing mutable Blueprint may now name one
exact published Template Version for the requests its future instantiations create, without any
Blueprint version history being invented. Selecting one and creating from one are separate
questions: an author may only select a currently published Version its own Blueprint owner holds,
while everything that later creates a request asks again and is refused by stable machine reason
when the named Version has since been retired. A retired reference stays stored, so the Blueprint
stays readable and the rest of it stays editable, and an update that says nothing about the Version
never revalidates it. A copy made for another owner starts without a name rather than carrying one
its new owner could not issue, and the platform is refused as a naming Blueprint owner because it
holds neither gate. `P2-T10` is now `P2-T10a` and `P2-T10b`, because rules that read only the
authored document and one already-stored Schema Version are a separate session from the typed
requirement first having to say which Field it collects. `P2-T10a` is complete and needed no
migration. A configuration that names a Schema Version is now held to naming one that exists, has
frozen, is written for `INFORMATION_REQUEST`, is not retired, and belongs to the Template's own
owner or to the platform, asked while the draft is authored and about the stored owner rather than
the caller. Within one requirement, everything stated about answering must be reachable by the party
the response mode nominates. `P2-T10b` is complete and allocated V91, so `P2-T10` is complete. A
requirement that asks for typed data now names the stable Field the answer is recorded against, a
requirement of any other kind names none, and one Version collects one Field once. Whether the

settled as the plain provided answer and nothing else rather than as every answer, which is the

type, tenant visibility, existing assignment state, resource lifecycle, and Schema management

The runtime Template materializer preflights recorded capability contracts, copies each frozen
Template binding into one root runtime Requirement occurrence and first append-only revision,
derives a stable SHA-256 configuration hash for that frozen policy, advances the current-revision
pointer, and delegates to the exact Fields assignment path only when the Template has Field

Acting party assignment now rejects unsupported principal kinds before creating a request-scoped

## Implementation Journal

### 2026-09-21: Personal and organization Information Request entitlement corrected

- Corrected the denial that reported Information Requests were excluded from Personal. The fixed
  plan catalog includes `INFORMATION_REQUESTS` in Personal, inherited by Business, while explicit
  platform-admin overrides can still withdraw or grant a feature for an owner.
- Personal Template reads and mutations now resolve both the personal owner and the active
  organization. Either eligible owner permits the Personal Settings scope, so organization members
  do not need individual grants. Organization scope still resolves only its organization, and
  Platform remains read-only.
- Personal schema selection now returns platform plus personally owned Schemas, never the active
  organization's Schemas. Personal Field-backed Information Requests no longer require the
  organization-only `BUSINESS_FIELDS_AND_SCHEMAS` feature at execution-grant issuance.
- Removed stale subscription-rollout assumptions from the active decision text. Historical task
  descriptions are superseded; platform-admin feature overrides are the only per-owner control.
- Verification: the focused backend command covering plan, access, Template guard/authoring/reference,
  execution grant, and Schema tenant-boundary behavior passed 107 tests with zero failures, errors,
  or skips. The first complete backend run exposed three obsolete tests that still expected a missing
  override to deny the now-included feature. After correcting those expectations, the affected three
  classes passed 31 tests and a clean `\.\mvnw.cmd test -DskipFrontend=true` rerun passed 2,569 tests
  with zero failures, errors, or skips. Focused frontend Settings/service tests passed 13 tests,
  including Personal-plan Settings visibility. `npx tsc --noEmit` passed.
- Help documentation now states Personal inclusion, active-organization sponsorship, Personal,
  Organization, and read-only Platform scopes, and personal/platform Schema selection. The article
  remains 148 lines. No migration, infrastructure, commit, or push was added.
- Phase 6 remains in progress. Its next task remains P6-T1b after this entitlement correction.

### 2026-09-12: `P5-R18` Frozen recipient-capacity reservations

- Current phase/task: Phase 5 remediation, `P5-R18` from finding 18.
- Status: complete. Read `AGENTS.md`, the active implementation plan status, plan/evidence update
  protocol, mandatory implementation protocol, latest implementation result, the companion evidence
  file, and `DOCUMENT-DRIVEN-INFORMATION-REQUESTS-PHASES-1-5-REVIEW.md` before starting. Inspected
  the dirty working tree and preserved unrelated changes. Phase 6 was not started. No commit or
  push was made.
- Problem:
  - `InformationRequestExecutionGrantService.issueGrant` froze owner-funded request capacity, but
    no production command spent that capacity through `InformationRequestExecutionUsageReservationService`.
  - Issuing a request with existing acting parties never reserved or consumed frozen recipient
    capacity.
  - Adding or revoking acting parties after issuance never consulted, consumed, released, or rolled
    back the request-local recipient cap.
- TDD red path:
  - Added focused production-caller regressions to `InformationRequestLifecycleServiceTest` and
    `InformationRequestPartyServiceTest`.
  - Initial sandboxed backend run failed before tests because the Maven wrapper could not connect:
    `Permission denied: connect`.
  - The first approved focused run reached test compilation and failed on a bad Mockito matcher
    import. That was not counted as the red state; the matcher was corrected.
  - Approved focused red run:
    `.\mvnw.cmd "-Dtest=InformationRequestLifecycleServiceTest,InformationRequestPartyServiceTest" test -DskipFrontend=true`
    reached the focused suites and failed with 35 tests, 3 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped. The
    failures were the intended missing reservation-service calls for issuance, issued acting-party
    assignment, and issued acting-party revocation.
- Implementation:
  - `InformationRequestLifecycleService` now receives `InformationRequestPartyRepository` and
    `InformationRequestExecutionUsageReservationService`.
  - Issuance calls `issueGrant`, loads active parties for the request, filters out the subject
    party, reserves one `ADDITIONAL_RECIPIENT` unit per acting party using a deterministic
    `information_request.party|{partyId}` key, and consumes each reservation.
  - If an issuance batch fails after any party capacity was reserved or consumed, the service
    releases unconsumed reservations and rolls back consumed reservations before rethrowing.
  - `InformationRequestPartyService` now receives `InformationRequestExecutionGrantService` and
    `InformationRequestExecutionUsageReservationService`.
  - Acting-party assignment on an already-issued request reserves capacity before creating the
    request-scoped Share, consumes after the party row is saved, and releases the unconsumed
    reservation if Share creation or later assignment work fails.
  - Assignment command receipt replay returns the stored party result and does not rerun capacity
    reservation or consumption.
  - Revoking an acting party on an issued request resolves the same deterministic reservation key
    and rolls back its consumed reservation, making the slot available for later assignment.
  - Draft party assignment remains grant-free; subject parties still create no Share and spend no
    recipient slot.
- Regression coverage added:
  - Issuing consumes frozen recipient capacity for active acting parties and skips the subject
    party.
  - Issuing rolls back an already-consumed party reservation when a later party exceeds the frozen
    cap, and the request row is not updated.
  - Assigning an acting party to an issued request reserves and consumes one frozen recipient slot.
  - Replaying the same issued assignment command with the same idempotency key does not reserve or
    consume twice.
  - If Share creation fails after reservation, the issued assignment releases the unconsumed
    reservation and does not save the party.
  - Revoking an issued acting party rolls back its consumed recipient slot.
- Focused production-caller regression:
  `.\mvnw.cmd "-Dtest=InformationRequestLifecycleServiceTest,InformationRequestPartyServiceTest" test -DskipFrontend=true`
  passed with 38 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped.

    value.

    sequence rather than directly seeding hidden state. Two interim focused reruns failed on test

    The expectations were corrected before the final focused run.

    evaluated.

    recorded principal, and recorded session reference.

    narrative, and no `fieldValueSetId`, so cleared current values are not resurrected.

    participates in the same request response revision/history update as other response changes.

  - `ARCHIVE_OUTSIDE_ACTIVE_RESPONSE` false to TRUE follows the same retained-answer transition.

### 2026-09-12: `P5-R15` Nested conditions and editor commands

- Current phase/task: Phase 5 remediation, `P5-R15` from finding 15.
- Status: complete. Read `AGENTS.md`, the active implementation plan status, plan/evidence update
  protocol, mandatory implementation protocol, latest implementation result, the companion evidence
  file, and `DOCUMENT-DRIVEN-INFORMATION-REQUESTS-PHASES-1-5-REVIEW.md` before starting. Inspected
  the dirty working tree and preserved unrelated changes. Phase 6 was not started. No commit or push
  was made.
- Problem:
  - `InformationRequestConditionEvaluationService.fieldValuesByScope` overlaid only root and exact
    occurrence Value Sets. A condition evaluated for `items[0]/entries[0]` could not read a Field
    collected at `items[0]`, so the rule returned `UNKNOWN`.
  - Disposition predicates had the same root-or-exact shape and did not search ancestor occurrence
    answers.
  - The structured-response workspace derived group identity from the first path segment, so a
    nested occurrence such as `reported-item[0]/entry[0]` behaved like the outer group.
  - The editor rendered only root-level add controls and omitted `parentOccurrenceId` when nested
    add or reorder commands were needed.
- TDD red path:
  - Added a backend regression in `InformationRequestConditionEvaluationServiceTest` proving a
    nested condition scope reads its own parent occurrence Field and does not cross into a sibling
    parent branch.
  - Initial sandboxed backend run failed before Maven could start because the wrapper needed
    user-directory or network access. Approved rerun reached the focused test.
  - Red backend run:
    `.\mvnw.cmd "-Dtest=InformationRequestConditionEvaluationServiceTest" test -DskipFrontend=true`
    failed with 8 tests, 1 failure, 0 errors, 0 skipped. The new test expected
    `items[0]/entries[0]` TRUE and `items[1]/entries[0]` FALSE, but both were `UNKNOWN`.
  - Added a frontend regression in `InformationRequestStructuredResponseWorkspace.test.tsx`
    rendering two parent branches and nested child occurrences. The test verifies a child add sends
    `{groupKey: "entry", parentOccurrenceId: "parent-1"}` and child reorder sends the same parent
    identity with only that parent's child occurrence IDs.
  - Initial sandboxed frontend run failed before Vitest could start because Node could not lstat the
    user directory. Approved rerun reached the focused test.
  - Red frontend run:
    `npm test -- InformationRequestStructuredResponseWorkspace.test.tsx --run` failed with 1 failed
    test because the expected nested child add control did not exist.
- Implementation:
  - `InformationRequestConditionEvaluationService` now builds occurrence scope ancestry from a path
    such as `items[0]/entries[0]` as `items[0]`, then `items[0]/entries[0]`.
  - Field predicate state now overlays root values, then ancestor occurrence values, then exact
    occurrence values, so nearer scopes override broader scopes while sibling branches remain
    isolated.
  - Disposition predicate state now resolves exact or ancestor occurrence answers from nearest to
    broadest before falling back to a single root answer. Ambiguous multiple answers at one scope
    remain unresolved instead of picking one.
  - `structuredResponseWorkspaceState.ts` now resolves an occurrence's group key from
    `sourceTemplateGroupId` and the Template group list, using path parsing only as a fallback, and
    computes siblings by `sourceTemplateGroupId` plus `parentOccurrenceId`.
  - `InformationRequestStructuredResponseWorkspace.tsx` now passes only root groups to the top
    toolbar and computes occurrence reorder position from scoped siblings rather than the whole
    rendered occurrence list.
  - `StructuredResponseOccurrence.tsx` now renders nested child add controls inside non-root parent
    occurrences, passes `parentOccurrenceId` through add and reorder commands, and uses the
    template group identity for Requirement filtering and reorder payloads.
  - The frontend test setup now mocks reorder command results so the nested reorder assertion does
    not leave an unhandled promise error.
- Regression coverage added:
  - Nested condition on child occurrence reads the parent occurrence's Field for the same branch.
  - A sibling parent branch with a different parent Field value evaluates independently.
  - Nested child add command includes the selected parent occurrence ID.
  - Nested child reorder command uses the nested group key, the selected parent occurrence ID, and
    only the child siblings under that parent.

  working tree and preserved unrelated changes. Phase 6 was not started. No commit or push was made.

  - `InformationRequestQueryService.findById` and the workspace load path still called
    `InformationRequestEntitlementGuard.requireRequestAccess`, so an issued request could become
    unreadable when the owner later lost live commercial entitlement or rollout access.

    authorization, so already-issued work and still-gated drafts were not separated.

  - Added a read-entitlement path that uses a present `RequestExecutionGrant` as the frozen
    commercial and rollout decision for runtime reads, matching the continuation-mutation contract.
  - Kept draft or never-issued request reads on the live owner `requireRequestAccess` gate.
  - Kept live operational suspension effective for issued reads through
    `requireNotOperationallySuspended`.
  - Kept explicit per-request operational revocation effective by refusing a grant whose
    `revokedAt` is set with `INFORMATION_REQUEST_EXECUTION_GRANT_REVOKED`.
  - Changed Exchange listing to apply the read entitlement per centrally visible request. This lets
    issued requests with frozen grants remain listed while never-issued drafts blocked by the live
    gate are omitted. If every centrally visible request is blocked by entitlement, the first
    entitlement refusal is surfaced rather than silently returning an empty list.
  - Removed the signed-in user's `usePlanFeature(PlanFeature.INFORMATION_REQUESTS)` gate from
    `InformationRequestStructuredResponsePanel`; the panel now renders the workspace once the server
    has returned the workspace payload for either an authenticated caller or an access-link session.

  - Issued request detail read bypasses a withdrawn live owner gate when a frozen grant exists.
  - Issued request detail read still checks live operational suspension.
  - Issued request detail read is denied when the frozen grant is explicitly revoked.
  - Exchange listing keeps issued work on a frozen grant while dropping drafts blocked by live gates.
  - Recipient-bound session style access reads issued work through the owner-funded frozen grant.

### 2026-09-12: `P5-R12` Contact proof attempts and bootstrap link accounting are enforced

- Current phase/task: Phase 5 remediation, `P5-R12` from finding 12.
- Status: complete. Read `AGENTS.md`, the active plan status, and the Phases 1-5 review before
  starting. Inspected the dirty working tree and preserved unrelated changes. Phase 6 was not
  started.
- Problem: contact proof OTP verification was not bounded by persisted attempt state, and verified
  bootstrap access consumed only `RequestAccessSession.useCount` while `ShareLink.maxUses`
  continued to check `ShareLink.usedCount`.
- Fix:
  `InformationRequestContactProofService.issueChallenge` and `verifyChallenge` now resolve the
  bootstrap ShareLink under a pessimistic row lock, enforce expiry and bootstrap `maxUses`, reject
  temporarily locked links, persist failed-attempt counts, set a lockout after repeated wrong codes,
  clear OTP and attempt state on success, and advance `ShareLink.usedCount` in the same transaction
  that mints the verified `RequestAccessSession`.
- Access behavior:
  challenge issuance and verification consume the bootstrap link capacity boundary, while
  session-authenticated request reads and response writes continue to validate the minted session
  credential without consuming additional bootstrap link uses. This keeps a one-use link from
  minting multiple sessions without stranding the session it already minted.
- Rotation behavior:
  `InformationRequestBootstrapShareLinkService.rotate` now clears persisted OTP attempt and lockout
  state when resetting a bootstrap link in place; replacement links start with the entity defaults.

### 2026-09-11: `P5-R11` Exact-party authorization follows linked accounts and current groups

- Current phase/task: Phase 5 remediation, `P5-R11` from finding 11.
- Status: complete. Read `AGENTS.md`, the active plan status, and the Phases 1-5 review before
  starting. Inspected the dirty working tree and preserved unrelated changes. Phase 6 was not
  started.
- Problem: exact-party Requirement authorization only matched the stored assigned party principal or
  active delegated authority. A participant who later registered through a verified
  `ParticipantAccountLink` could lose assigned Requirement read/respond access because the party
  principal remained `PARTICIPANT`. A User who was a current active member of an assigned
  `PRINCIPAL_GROUP` party could also be denied because group membership was not represented in the
  Requirement assignment facts.
- TDD red test: added linked registered User and active group member cases to
  `InformationRequestRequirementPolicyEvaluatorTest`. The red command
  `.\mvnw.cmd "-Dtest=InformationRequestRequirementPolicyEvaluatorTest#linked registered User may respond for a participant assigned party+linked registered User may view a participant assigned Requirement+active group member may respond for an assigned group party+removed group member is denied when not present in current assignment facts" test -DskipFrontend=true`
  failed as intended with 4 tests run, 3 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped. The failures were the linked
  registered User respond/read paths and the active group member respond path. The removed-member
  denial already passed.
- Implementation: `InformationRequestRequirementAssignedPartyFact` now carries
  `equivalentPrincipals` in addition to the stored party `principal`. The authorization context
  provider populates that set from `ParticipantAccountLinkRepository.findByParticipantId` for
  participant parties and from `PrincipalGroupMemberRepository.findActiveMembers` for group parties.
  Active User group members are included directly, active participant group members include both the
  participant principal and any verified linked User, and unsupported nested group members are not
  expanded. The evaluator now accepts a caller whose principal equals the stored party principal, is
  present in `equivalentPrincipals`, or has active delegated authority for the same party ID.
- Provenance and scope: the original assigned party principal, party ID, role key, subject identity,
  Exchange recipient ID, and Share ID remain in the fact. Linked accounts and group members are
  authorization equivalents only; the assignment is not rewritten to a different principal.

  User members, active participant group members include their linked User, unsupported nested group

### 2026-09-11: `P5-R10` Stable occurrence identity stays unique after removal and reorder

- Current phase/task: Phase 5 remediation, `P5-R10` from finding 10.
- Status: complete. Read `AGENTS.md`, the active plan status, and the Phases 1-5 review before
  starting. Inspected the dirty working tree and preserved unrelated changes. Phase 6 was not
  started.
- Problem: repeatable group occurrence `occurrenceIndex` was serving both as display order and as
  the stable identity used in occurrence paths. After a removal and reorder, a remaining active
  occurrence could have display index `0` while retaining stable path `items[1]`; adding the next
  occurrence could reuse `items[1]`, collide with history, and provision Field Value Sets under the
  wrong path.
- TDD red test: added
  `adding after removal and reorder keeps a new stable occurrence path` to
  `InformationRequestGroupOccurrenceServiceTest`. The red command
  `.\mvnw.cmd "-Dtest=InformationRequestGroupOccurrenceServiceTest#adding after removal and reorder keeps a new stable occurrence path" test -DskipFrontend=true`
  failed as intended with expected `items[2]` but actual `items[1]`.
- Implementation: `InformationRequestGroupOccurrenceRepository` now has
  `findForGroupAndParentForUpdate`, locking every sibling occurrence row for the request, group, and
  parent path, including removed rows. `InformationRequestGroupOccurrenceService.addOccurrence`
  derives mutable display order from active siblings and derives stable identity from every existing
  sibling occurrence path. Occurrence creation now receives display index and identity index
  separately, so the stored `occurrenceIndex` can remain display order while `occurrencePath` stays a
  non-reused stable identity.

  `group occurrence display order can change while stable paths remain unique` to
  `InformationRequestRuntimePersistenceContractTest`. It inserts a removed `items[0]`, a reordered
  active `items[1]`, an added active `items[2]`, verifies active display ordering, and keeps the

### 2026-09-11: `P5-R09` Response DTOs expose Template correlation for structured saves

- Status: complete. Read `AGENTS.md`, the active plan's `## Status`, and the Phases 1-5 review before
  starting. Inspected the working tree and preserved unrelated modified/untracked changes. Phase 6
  was not started.
- Finding 9 failure mode: the structured response workspace selected a runtime Requirement for a
  Field binding by checking whether a response's whole Value Set contained that Field. That is
  ambiguous for sparse responses because every response in the same root or repeated occurrence can
  point at the same Value Set, so editing only the second Field in an occurrence could save against
  the first runtime Requirement, and editing both Fields in the same occurrence could name the same
  runtime Requirement twice.

### 2026-09-11: `P5-R08` Multi-Field saves in one occurrence batch into one Fields mutation

- Status: complete. Read `AGENTS.md`, the active plan's `## Status`, and the Phases 1-5 review before
  starting. `git status` showed the same pre-existing unrelated modified/untracked paths from earlier
  sessions listed in the prior journal entry; none were touched by this task.
- Finding 8 described
  [InformationRequestResponseDraftService.kt:191](../src/main/kotlin/com/docuhyphen/app/api/service/informationrequest/InformationRequestResponseDraftService.kt):
  patching two different Field Requirements that collect Fields in the same root or repeated Value
  Set, both against the ETag the workspace served, failed. `mutate()`'s per-patch loop called
  `SchemaAssignmentService.setValues` once per Requirement; the first call advanced the shared Value
  Set's revision, so the second call's precondition -- naming the same original ETag the client
  legitimately read -- was judged stale against the revision the first call had just produced,
  aborting the whole command. Existing coverage (`field patch writes the occurrence through Fields...`,
  `patch across two occurrences writes each occurrence's Field values independently`) only exercised
  one Requirement per occurrence or Requirements in different occurrences, so it never reached the
  two-Requirements-one-occurrence path that actually conflicts with itself.
- Investigation before changing anything: read `InformationRequestResponseDraftService.mutate` and
  `writeFieldValues`, `SchemaAssignmentService.writeValues` (`setValues`), and `FieldsPrecondition`.
  Confirmed `writeValues` already accepts a list of entries and checks its precondition exactly once
  per call against the addressed `FieldValueSet`'s current revision -- the defect was entirely in the
  caller submitting one command per Requirement instead of one command per Value Set, not in the
  Fields engine itself. Confirmed `FieldsPrecondition.ExpectedRevision` is a `data class` over a
  `Set<String>` of acceptable ETags, so its instances compare by value and are safe to compare for
  equality across patches addressing the same occurrence.
- Fix: added `writeBatchedFieldValues`, replacing the per-patch `writeFieldValues` call inside
  `mutate()`. It filters to patches carrying `fieldValues`, validates every entry's Field binding
  against its own Requirement first (unchanged `requireEntriesBoundToRequirement` behavior, now run
  for all field patches before any write), groups the remaining patches by the `FieldValueSetRef`
  their Requirement's occurrence resolves to, then submits exactly one `FieldValueWriteCommand` per
  group with every group member's entries concatenated in patch order. A new `mergeFieldPreconditions`
  requires every patch in a group to carry the identical `FieldsPrecondition` (structural equality) and
  throws `STRUCTURED_RESPONSE_VALIDATION_FAILED` otherwise, rather than silently picking one and
  masking a real client-side inconsistency; in practice every patch addressing one occurrence in one
  PATCH call carries the one ETag the workspace served for it, so this never fires for a well-formed
  client. The resulting `FieldResponsePatchResult` (Value Set id, projection, changed flag) from each
  group's single `setValues` call is shared by every Requirement in that group, matching the existing
  per-Requirement Field projection filtering in `activeFieldProjection`, which already narrows the
  shared occurrence-wide projection down to each Requirement's own collected Field. `mutate()`'s
  authorize/disposition/revision-presence checks for every patch now run in their own pass before any
  Field write, so a malformed patch is rejected before any Fields mutation is attempted for any
  Requirement, rather than after some earlier Requirement in the loop had already been written.
- TDD:
  1. Added three tests to `InformationRequestResponseDraftServiceTest`: `two Field Requirement patches
     in the same occurrence batch into one Fields mutation instead of conflicting with each other's
     precondition` (two Requirements sharing `occurrencePath = "items[0]"`, same precondition, asserts
     exactly one `setValues` call with both entries merged in order), `an explicit clear entry batches
     with a normal Field entry addressing the same occurrence` (one kept entry, one `JsonNull` clear
     entry, same occurrence, asserts one merged `setValues` call), and `a stale precondition on one
     occurrence's batched Field write rolls back the whole patch including an already written sibling
     occurrence` (two Requirements in different occurrences; the second occurrence's `setValues` throws
     `FieldsPreconditionException.stale`; asserts no response, request, or history side effect from
     either occurrence).
  2. Confirmed all three would fail for the intended reason: temporarily reverted
     `InformationRequestResponseDraftService` to the original per-patch loop (verified byte-identical
     restoration afterward via `diff`) and reran the class against that reverted production code. The
     two same-occurrence tests failed with Mockito `TooManyActualInvocations` (`setValues` called
     twice instead of once, with mismatched merged-entries assertions). The rollback test failed a
     different way that itself demonstrates the old code's defect: the old per-patch loop interleaves
     each patch's Field write with that same patch's response persistence, so patch one (occurrence
     `items[0]`) fully saved its response envelope into the mocked `responseStore` before patch two
     (occurrence `items[1]`) threw the stale-precondition exception; `assertTrue(fixture.responses
     .isEmpty())` then failed (`expected true but was false`) because patch one's response was already
     present. The new code performs every group's Field write in `writeBatchedFieldValues` before any
     response is persisted, so no such partial mock-visible side effect exists even without a real
     transactional rollback. Restored the fix and confirmed all 24 tests in the class pass.
  3. Removed the now-dead single-patch `writeFieldValues` function; no other file referenced it
     (confirmed by search).
- Focused regression: `.\mvnw.cmd -Dtest=InformationRequestResponseDraftServiceTest test`: 24 tests
  (21 pre-existing plus the 3 new), 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped.
- Full backend regression: `.\mvnw.cmd test` with Docker/Postgres available: 2519 tests, 0 failures, 1
  error, 0 skipped. The one error is the same unchanged `P5-R19` delegated-authority fixture

### 2026-09-11: `P5-R07` Removed occurrence subtrees excluded from active state; requirement-level write denial closed

- Status: complete. Read `AGENTS.md`, the active plan's `## Status`, and the Phases 1-5 review before
  starting. `git status` showed only pre-existing unrelated modified/untracked paths from earlier
  sessions; none were touched by this task.
- Finding 7 described
  [InformationRequestCompletenessProgressService.kt:44](../src/main/kotlin/com/docuhyphen/app/api/service/informationrequest/InformationRequestCompletenessProgressService.kt):
  removing a repeatable group occurrence only stamps `removed_at` and keeps its Requirement rows for
  history, but completeness, response saves, condition evaluation, and the workspace were said to
  load every Requirement row unfiltered, so a removed occurrence's Requirement kept counting toward
  the denominator, kept accepting writes, and kept evaluating conditions.
- Investigation before changing anything: read
  `InformationRequestCompletenessProgressService`, `InformationRequestConditionEvaluationService`,
  `InformationRequestResponseDraftService`, `InformationRequestResponseWorkspaceService`, and their
  test files. All four already build an `activeOccurrencePaths` set from
  `InformationRequestGroupOccurrenceRepository.findForRequest` (which already filters
  `removedAt IS NULL` at the SQL layer) and filter Requirements through the existing
  `InformationRequestOccurrencePath.isActiveOccurrence` helper; `InformationRequestResponseDraftService.mutate`
  additionally rejects any patch entry naming a Requirement outside that active set with the existing
  `InformationRequestErrorCatalog.GROUP_OCCURRENCE_REMOVED` code. Each of these already has passing
  regression coverage: `InformationRequestCompletenessProgressServiceTest` (`a removed occurrence's
  requirement is excluded from completeness though its row still exists`,
  `removing a parent occurrence also excludes its nested descendant subtree from completeness`),
  `InformationRequestConditionEvaluationServiceTest` (`a removed occurrence is excluded from a rule's
  scopes and evaluation falls back to root`), `InformationRequestResponseWorkspaceServiceTest` (`a
  removed occurrence's requirement is excluded from the workspace though its row still exists`),
  `InformationRequestResponseDraftServiceTest` (asserts `GROUP_OCCURRENCE_REMOVED` on a patch
  targeting a removed occurrence's Requirement), and `InformationRequestGroupOccurrenceServiceTest`
  (`removing an occurrence marks it removed and keeps prior requirement history addressable`,
  `removing an occurrence authorizes its own and its descendants' occurrence paths before mutating`,
  `a stale response-shape precondition refuses before touching group occurrences`). None of this was
  newly written by this session; it predates this task and the finding's own wording, so it is
  recorded here rather than reimplemented or reasserted as new work.
- Residual gap found by inspection: `InformationRequestRequirementAuthorizationContextProvider.resolve`
  builds `InformationRequestRequirementPolicyFacts` purely from the Requirement and its current
  revision, with no occurrence-removal check at all. Every Field write for an Information Request
  also flows through the generic Fields engine's per-binding policy,
  [InformationRequestFieldBindingPolicy.decide](../src/main/kotlin/com/docuhyphen/app/api/service/informationrequest/InformationRequestFieldBindingPolicy.kt),
  registered as the request resource type's `FieldResourceAdapter.bindingPolicy` in
  `InformationRequestFieldResourceAdapter`. That policy authorizes each write against
  `Action.INFORMATION_REQUEST_REQUIREMENT_RESPOND` on `ResourceRef.informationRequestRequirement(id)`
  through the central `InformationRequestRequirementPolicyEvaluator`, entirely independent of
  `InformationRequestResponseDraftService.mutate`'s own `GROUP_OCCURRENCE_REMOVED` check. A caller who
  holds `RESPOND` on some other still-active Requirement in the same request (the central authorizer's
  own aggregate/resource-level grant check, unrelated to the specific occurrence) could therefore
  still write a Field value anchored at a removed occurrence's Value Set through the generic Fields
  endpoint, bypassing the response-patch-specific rejection. This is the part of finding 7 ("the
  Requirement context does not deny removed occurrences") that remained open.
- Fix:
  - Added `occurrenceRemoved: Boolean = false` to `InformationRequestRequirementPolicyFacts`.
  - `InformationRequestRequirementAuthorizationContextProvider.requirementPolicyFacts` (the `resolve`
    path, used for a real materialized Requirement) now loads the same active-occurrence-path set via
    `InformationRequestGroupOccurrenceRepository.findForRequest` and computes `occurrenceRemoved` with
    `InformationRequestOccurrencePath.isActiveOccurrence` against the current revision's occurrence
    path, mirroring the pattern already used in the four services above.
    `authoredPolicyFacts` (the `authoredContextFor` path used by `P5-R06`'s
    `InformationRequestGroupAuthorizationService` for a not-yet-materialized binding, where there is
    no real occurrence to check) always passes `occurrenceRemoved = false`; an authored, not-yet-added
    occurrence is not a removed one, and treating it as removed would have wrongly denied the
    zero-occurrence add path `P5-R06` just fixed.
  - `InformationRequestRequirementPolicyEvaluator.evaluateWithFacts` now denies with the existing
    `GROUP_OCCURRENCE_REMOVED` code whenever `facts.occurrenceRemoved` is true and the requested
    action is one of the existing `answerMutationActions` (`RESPOND`, `ATTEST`, `EVIDENCE_UPLOAD`,
    `EVIDENCE_WITHDRAW`). View actions are deliberately left unaffected, so a historical read through
    this same path stays permitted, consistent with "preserve history" and with the fact that the
    response projections already exclude removed occurrences from what gets shown as *active*.
- TDD:
  1. Added two tests to `InformationRequestRequirementPolicyEvaluatorTest`: `a removed group
     occurrence's Requirement denies response mutation` (`RESPOND` with `occurrenceRemoved = true`
     denies with `GROUP_OCCURRENCE_REMOVED`) and `a removed group occurrence's Requirement still
     permits a historical view` (`VIEW` with `occurrenceRemoved = true` still permits). Confirmed
     both would fail before the evaluator change: the first returned `Permit` (no removal check
     existed), and the second was written to prove the fix does not overreach.
  2. Added three tests to `InformationRequestRequirementAuthorizationContextProviderTest`: `a removed
     occurrence's Requirement context marks occurrenceRemoved true` (stubs an empty active-occurrence
     list and asserts `resolve` produces `occurrenceRemoved = true`), `an active occurrence's
     Requirement context marks occurrenceRemoved false` (the default fixture, where the occurrence is
     present and active), and `an authored binding with no materialized occurrence yet is never marked
     occurrenceRemoved` (`authoredContextFor` with an empty active-occurrence list still returns
     `occurrenceRemoved = false`, proving the zero-occurrence add path from `P5-R06` is unaffected).
     Confirmed the first would fail before the provider change (facts had no such field/behavior).
  3. Added `occurrenceRepository` (`InformationRequestGroupOccurrenceRepository`) as a new
     constructor dependency on `InformationRequestRequirementAuthorizationContextProvider` and updated
     every existing direct instantiation:
     `InformationRequestRequirementAuthorizationContextProviderTest` (stubs the occurrence matching

### 2026-09-11: `P5-R06` Group command authorization against the authored group and Requirement scope

- Status: complete. Read `AGENTS.md`, the active plan, and the Phases 1-5 review before starting.
  `git status` showed only pre-existing unrelated modified/untracked paths from earlier sessions;
  none were touched by this task.
- Finding 6 described
  [InformationRequestGroupOccurrenceService.kt:366](../src/main/kotlin/com/docuhyphen/app/api/service/informationrequest/InformationRequestGroupOccurrenceService.kt):
  `add`, `remove`, and `reorder` all authorized only `INFORMATION_REQUEST_REQUIREMENT_RESPOND`
  against `ResourceRef.informationRequest(requestId)`, the coarse aggregate request-level grant, so
  the `InformationRequestRequirementPolicyEvaluator` that enforces exact party assignment, response
  mode, confidentiality, correction scope, and request state never ran for a group command. A
  CONTRIBUTOR with aggregate response capability could add, remove, or reorder occurrences of a
  group whose Requirements are assigned to PREPARER, are NOT_DISCLOSED, or sit in a protected
  confidentiality compartment.
- Fix: added `InformationRequestGroupAuthorizationService` and wired it into all three commands in
  `InformationRequestGroupOccurrenceService`, in addition to (not instead of) the existing coarse
  check, which still establishes that the actor holds some grant on the request at all:
  - `authorizeOccurrenceScope(access, requestId, occurrencePaths)` loads the request's
    `InformationRequestRequirement` rows, filters to the given occurrence paths, and authorizes each
    one via `ResourceRef.informationRequestRequirement(id)` (the same call
    `InformationRequestResponseDraftService` already uses), throwing `ForbiddenException` on any
    deny. `remove` calls this with the target occurrence's path plus every descendant occurrence
    path (mirroring the existing removal-subtree walk) before marking anything removed; `reorder`
    calls it with every active sibling's path before applying the new order.
  - `authorizeMaterializedBindings(access, request, bindings)` handles `add`, which creates
    Requirement rows rather than touching existing ones. For each Template binding the command will
    materialize (the group's own anchored binding, plus any descendant group's anchored bindings
    whose authored minimum occurrences also materialize immediately, mirrored from
    `materializeChildMinimums` as a new `TemplateData.materializedBindings` helper), it authorizes
    against an existing `InformationRequestRequirement` sharing that binding when one already exists
    elsewhere in the request (policy facts are binding- and request-scoped, not occurrence-scoped,
    so any existing instance of the same binding yields the same decision); when none exists yet
    (a zero-occurrence group's first occurrence), it instead calls a new
    `InformationRequestRequirementAuthorizationContextProvider.authoredContextFor(request, binding)`
    that builds the same `InformationRequestRequirementPolicyFacts` a materialized Requirement would
    carry (assigned parties, response mode, confidentiality, correction scope, parent snapshot) using
    a freshly generated requirement id, then evaluates them directly through the same
    `InformationRequestRequirementPolicyEvaluator` bean, so a not-yet-materialized binding can no
    longer be authorized by falling back to the coarse aggregate grant.
  - Refactored `InformationRequestRequirementAuthorizationContextProvider` to extract the shared
    facts-building logic (`buildFacts`) used by both the existing `resolve(resourceId)` path (a real
    Requirement and its current revision) and the new `authoredContextFor` path (a binding with no
    materialized Requirement yet); behavior of `resolve` is unchanged.
  - Both scoped checks run after the query/validation steps that establish the affected scope but
    before any entity mutation, so a denial leaves the transaction with nothing changed.

### 2026-09-10: `P5-R05` Field audience and purpose boundaries against the actual caller and owner

- Status: complete. Read `AGENTS.md`, the active plan's `## Status`, update protocols, the Phases
  1-5 review, and the `P5-R04` completion evidence before starting. Confirmed `git status` showed
  only unrelated pre-existing working-tree changes (490 modified/untracked paths across the
  repository from earlier sessions); none were touched by this task.
- Finding 5 described two related gaps in
  [InformationRequestFieldBindingPolicy.kt](../src/main/kotlin/com/docuhyphen/app/api/service/informationrequest/InformationRequestFieldBindingPolicy.kt):
  `isExternalCaller` always returned `false`, so the shared `AudienceFieldBindingPolicy` rule that
  limits an outside caller to `PUBLIC`-classified bindings never engaged for any Information Request
  caller; and when `requirementIdAnswering` found no Requirement collecting the addressed Field
  Definition at the addressed occurrence, `decide()` fell through to that same (permissive) shared
  decision instead of recognizing that a respondent has no request-scoped purpose for an unbound
  Field at all.
- Fix:
  - `isExternalCaller` now resolves the caller's real relationship to the request's owner, mirroring
    [ExchangeFieldBindingPolicy.kt](../src/main/kotlin/com/docuhyphen/app/api/service/exchange/ExchangeFieldBindingPolicy.kt):
    `PARTICIPANT`/`PUBLIC_LINK` principals are always external; a `USER` principal is external unless
    an active `OrganizationMembershipRepository.findActiveByUserAndOrg` record ties them to the
    request's `ownerOrganizationId`, or they are the request's own `ownerUserId` for a personally
    owned request; every other principal kind is treated as internal. This needed two new
    constructor dependencies, `InformationRequestRepository` and `OrganizationMembershipRepository`
    (both already existed and are used identically by the Exchange policy).
  - `decide()` now branches explicitly when `requirementIdAnswering` returns `null`: an external
    caller is refused (`FieldBindingDecision.Deny(FieldBindingDenial.OUT_OF_AUDIENCE)`) regardless of
    the binding's classification, since an uncollected Field carries no explicitly authorized request
    purpose for a respondent; an internal (owner-side) caller keeps the prior shared-audience-rule
    outcome. Both reads and writes go through this same `decide()` call (`FieldBindingGate.permits`
    for the read-side Value Set projection, `FieldBindingGate.decide` for writes, both in
    `SchemaAssignmentService.kt`), so the fix filters projections and writes consistently by
    construction rather than needing a second code path.
- TDD:
  1. Added three tests to `InformationRequestFieldBindingPolicyTest`: an unregistered
     (`PrincipalRef.participant`) respondent denied an uncollected `INTERNAL` Field; a registered
     `USER` respondent who is not an active member of the owning organization denied an uncollected
     `CONFIDENTIAL` Field for both read and write; and an active owner-organization member retaining
     read access to an uncollected Field. Command:
     `.\mvnw.cmd -o surefire:test "-Dtest=InformationRequestFieldBindingPolicyTest"`.
  2. Confirmed the intended red state by temporarily reverting `isExternalCaller` to `= false` and
     the `decide()` no-Requirement branch to `?: return sharedDecision` (the pre-fix shape), then
     recompiling and rerunning the same selector: 2 of the 11 tests failed with
     `expected: <Deny(reason=OUT_OF_AUDIENCE)> but was: <Allow>` for both the unregistered-respondent
     and the outside-organization-respondent cases (the third, owner-access, case does not exercise
     the changed branch and passed either way) -- the correct behavioral reason, not a compilation or
     unrelated failure. Restored the fix; recompiled; the same selector passed 11/11.
  3. All 7 pre-existing tests in the file needed their direct
     `InformationRequestFieldBindingPolicy(...)` construction extended with the two new constructor
     parameters. A shared `internalRequestRepository()`/`internalMembershipRepository()` test helper
     pair stubs an owner-organization-member caller by default, so every pre-existing test (which
     exercises Requirement-level authorization, not audience) keeps its original, unchanged
     assertions and behavior.

     `InformationRequestFieldBindingPolicy` for one of its own dependencies; updated that single
     construction site to supply `mock()` for both new parameters. No behavioral assertion in that
     file exercises the binding policy itself, so nothing else in it changed.

### 2026-09-10: `P5-R04` exact Field binding and occurrence authorization

- Status: complete. Read `AGENTS.md`, the active plan's `## Status`, update protocols, and the
  Phases 1-5 review before starting. Verified the working tree and the `P5-R03` completion evidence
  matched the active plan's claimed state before resuming. Unrelated changes were preserved.
- Finding 4 described two related gaps in
  [InformationRequestFieldBindingPolicy.kt](../src/main/kotlin/com/docuhyphen/app/api/service/informationrequest/InformationRequestFieldBindingPolicy.kt):
  `requirementIdAnswering` picked the first Requirement anywhere on the request whose Template
  binding collects the addressed Field Definition, ignoring `FieldBindingAccess.valueSet` entirely.
  For a repeated Field bound once per occurrence of a group, this let a Fields write or read
  targeting one occurrence (for example `items[1]`) be authorized against a different occurrence's
  Requirement (`items[0]`), in either direction: a delegate scoped to only one occurrence could reach
  another, and a delegate correctly scoped to the addressed occurrence could be wrongly denied
  because resolution stopped at an unrelated sibling first.
- Fix: `requirementIdAnswering` now takes the caller's `FieldValueSetRef` and only accepts a
  Requirement whose own `occurrencePath` answers that exact value (`InformationRequestOccurrencePath.isRoot`
  for `FieldValueSetRef.Root`, or an exact path match for `FieldValueSetRef.Occurrence`), in addition
  to matching the Field Definition. A new private `answersOccurrence` helper expresses that match.
  Central authorization is then asked about the exact Requirement occurrence the caller addressed,
  never a sibling.
- The review separately noted that even with occurrence-scoped authorization, "the outer response
  patch does not bind each supplied Field entry to the patch's Requirement, so the broader occurrence
  mistake remains reachable": two Requirements sharing one occurrence but collecting different Fields
  could still let a patch declared against Requirement A carry a Field entry that actually answers
  sibling Requirement B at the same occurrence, since `writeFieldValues` derived its `valueSet` only
  from the patch's own Requirement and never checked that the entries themselves named that
  Requirement's own Field. Fixed in
  [InformationRequestResponseDraftService.kt](../src/main/kotlin/com/docuhyphen/app/api/service/informationrequest/InformationRequestResponseDraftService.kt):
  a new `requireEntriesBoundToRequirement` runs before any Fields write and rejects an entry whose
  Field Definition (resolved from its `fieldContractId` through the newly injected
  `FieldContractRepository`) does not equal the named Requirement's own `collectedFieldDefinitionId`
  (resolved from its `InformationRequestTemplateRequirementBinding` through the existing
  `bindingRepository`). The new refusal uses a new stable code,
  `InformationRequestErrorCatalog.FIELD_ENTRY_NOT_BOUND`
  (`INFORMATION_REQUEST_FIELD_ENTRY_NOT_BOUND`), added to the catalog and its `allCodes()` list.
- TDD:
  1. Added two failing tests to `InformationRequestFieldBindingPolicyTest`: one asserting a repeated
     Field write against `items[1]` is authorized against `items[1]`'s Requirement and never
     `items[0]`'s, one asserting a delegate authorized only for `items[0]` cannot have that
     authorization reused to write `items[1]`. Command:
     `.\mvnw.cmd -q -Dtest=InformationRequestFieldBindingPolicyTest test`. Both failed for the
     intended reason: the first because `authorize` was invoked with `items[0]`'s Requirement id
     instead of `items[1]`'s (Mockito argument mismatch), the second because the write was wrongly
     allowed (`Allow` instead of the expected `Deny(OUT_OF_AUDIENCE)`). `target` logs were not
     separately saved for this focused run; the failure output is reproduced above in this entry's
     drafting session and in the tool transcript.
  2. Implemented `answersOccurrence` and the `valueSet` parameter on `requirementIdAnswering`. Reran
     the same selector: 6 tests passed, 0 failures.
  3. Added a failing test to `InformationRequestResponseDraftServiceTest` for a Field entry naming a
     Field outside the named Requirement's collected Field, expecting
     `InformationRequestErrorCatalog.FIELD_ENTRY_NOT_BOUND`. Confirmed the intended red state by

### 2026-09-10: `P5-R03` hidden response projections and current Field clearing

- Status: complete. Resumed the saved work after verifying the implementation and logs
  were intact. The newer `P5-R02` continuation evidence and its completed regressions were verified
  before starting this next dependency-ready remediation. Unrelated changes were preserved.
- Active workspace responses now require a TRUE condition for their exact occurrence (with the
  existing root fallback) and an active response envelope. FALSE, UNKNOWN, missing evaluations,
  and retained inactive envelopes cannot expose Field values. Each response carries only its
  collected Field, and the workspace schema carries editor bindings without duplicate current
  values. The same projection filtering applies to saved and replayed Field representations.
- Confirmed hidden clears run even when the command contains no new answer patches. They resolve
  the exact collected Field in its Value Set, authorize the Requirement, and clear current values
  through the Fields engine with the current Field ETag. Missing or inaccessible Fields fail closed.
  Earlier Field revisions and canonical principal/session provenance remain; the response envelope
  is detached only after the Field clear succeeds. Directly stored Fields without an envelope can
  receive a hidden empty envelope after clearing.
- Conditions are reevaluated after each hidden-response mutation pass so clearing a source Field
  also applies the configured policy to newly hidden dependent Requirements. Each changed Requirement
  is processed once, bounding the pass count; dependent clears still require explicit confirmation
  inside the same transaction.
- Added an internal `FieldValueClearCommand` and `SchemaAssignmentService.clearValues` operation.
  It shares the ordinary Fields authorization, lifecycle, subscription, locking, precondition,
  validation, audit, and revision recorder. Explicit clearing can empty a required Schema Field;
  ordinary value saves retain required-value validation. No new HTTP endpoint or migration was added.
- This does not close `P5-R04`, `P5-R05`, `P5-R13`, or `P5-R16`: exact occurrence authorization,
  audience policy, consistent receipt representations, and response reactivation remain in their
  own unchecked remediation tasks. No Phase 6 work was started.

### 2026-09-10: `P5-R02` parent Exchange termination effects on runtime access

- Status: complete. `P5-R02` was the first dependency-ready unchecked remediation. No Phase 6 work
  was started. `P5-R03` is now the exact next task; findings 3-20 and `P5-R-GATE` remain open.
- Inherited work: an interrupted earlier session on the same day had already left uncommitted
  `P5-R02` production code in the working tree (child lifecycle service, parent policy facts,
  Exchange wiring, owner-read retention, request listing filter) with its own logs under
  `target/p5-r02-*.log`. That session stopped after a regression run that showed one failing
  existing test, and it never updated the plan or evidence. This session verified that code against
  its tests, resolved the failing contract, added the missing end-to-end and concurrency coverage,
  and completed the task. Unrelated working-tree changes, AGENTS.md, the proposal, and the original
  review were preserved. No commit or push was made.

Implementation:

- `InformationRequestParentLifecycleService` applies `InformationRequestTransitionMatrix.parentEffects`
  transactionally (`TxType.MANDATORY`) inside the Exchange transition. It flushes pending changes,
  locks each child request row, retains an owner read grant for a personally owned request, revokes
  every `RequestAccessSession` for the request when the effect is `REVOKE_ALL` or `REVOKE_NON_OWNER`,
  and cancels each non-terminal request with an append-only transition record whose reason code names
  the parent transition. Deletion preserves the recorded request state; ending changes no state.
- `ExchangeUpdateService` calls it on the direct status write, the acceptance-workflow routed
  decision, rescission, deletion, and both no-auth status paths, before Exchange shares are revoked,
  so the retained owner grant survives the revocation. `ExchangeApprovalEventHandler` calls it on the
  workflow-driven transitions. Exchange share revocation only covers Exchange-scoped Shares, so
  request-scoped Shares survive; the read policy, not share revocation, is what denies a party.
- The parent snapshot is now a resource policy fact. `ExchangeLifecycleStateService.snapshot`
  supplies it, `InformationRequestAuthorizationContextProvider` and
  `InformationRequestRequirementAuthorizationContextProvider` attach it, and
  `InformationRequestParentPolicy` maps the caller to OWNER or PARTY and applies
  `InformationRequestTransitionMatrix.canRead` for read actions and the terminal-parent refusal for
  every other action. `InformationRequestPolicyEvaluator` and
  `InformationRequestRequirementPolicyEvaluator` both run it, and both fail closed with
  `FactsUnavailable` when the parent cannot be resolved. Because the authenticated and no-auth
  surfaces build the same `RequestAccessContext` and call the same application services, one policy
  covers both. Session issuance separately locks the parent and refuses when the matrix denies
  external-session reads, so a terminated parent cannot mint a new respondent session.
- `InformationRequestQueryService.listForExchange` now authorizes every listed request individually
  instead of returning the Exchange's whole request set after one Exchange-level check. A caller
  denied on the Exchange but still permitted on a request (the owner whose Exchange Share was revoked
  by deletion) keeps that historical read; a caller denied everywhere is refused before the
  entitlement gate. This replaced the earlier expectation that a denied caller never reaches the
  request repository, which is no longer expressible once request-scoped access must be consulted.
- New in this session: all three request-mutation commands (`InformationRequestLifecycleService`,
  `InformationRequestResponseDraftService`, `InformationRequestGroupOccurrenceService`) locked the
  request row before the parent Exchange row, while termination locks the Exchange first and the
  request rows second. That inverted order is a deadlock under concurrent commands. A new
  `lockParentExchangeOf` helper gives every command one parent-first lock order, keeping the same
  `NOT_FOUND` and `PARENT_STATE_INVALID` refusals and the same precondition and authorization
  sequence afterwards.
- No migration was added or changed. No new AWS service or paid resource type was introduced.

### 2026-09-10: `P5-R01` independent recipient session credentials

- Status: complete. Implementation and tests ran 2026-09-09. After the session interruption,
  resumed on 2026-09-10 and verified all 36 implementation/test/configuration/help paths and
  completed test logs were intact before continuing. Unrelated working-tree changes, AGENTS.md,
  the proposal, and the original review were preserved. No commit or push was made.
- Dependency decision: `P5-R01` was the first unchecked, dependency-ready remediation. No Phase 6
  work was started. `P5-R02` is now the exact next task; findings 2-20 and `P5-R-GATE` remain open.

Implementation:

- Contact-proof issuance returns `IssuedRequestAccessSession` with a separately generated 32-byte
  SecureRandom secret, encoded as session ID plus base64url secret. The entity stores only a
  SHA-256 credential hash. Secret verification uses constant-time digest comparison. Malformed,
  missing, guessed, ID-only, expired, revoked, and non-expiring sessions fail closed.
- Session expiry is the earliest of the requested expiry, bootstrap expiry, and 24 hours. Runtime
  no-auth reads and mutations require the new `X-Request-Session-Token` header as well as the
  bootstrap token. The shared resolver validates secret/liveness, the bootstrap link and its active
  party, and the factory validates the exact link and recipient kind/ID. Every content resource
  also checks that the resolved party's request matches the URL. Removed the latest-session-by-link
  lookup and the old tests that treated it as authorization.
- Authenticated request access still uses the normal explicit principal and shared services.
  Registration upgrade now authenticates the session secret before mutation or receipt lookup and
  compares it with the requested session ID. An expired or revoked session cannot replay an upgrade;
  after a successful upgrade revokes its no-auth session, subsequent access uses the account.
  Command/result models were moved into the dedicated model package; command stringification omits
  the secret. Session issuance is the only API response containing the new secret and uses no-store.
- Tab-scoped session storage keeps the secret separate from the bootstrap link. All workspace,
  sparse response, and add/remove/reorder calls attach the credential. Opening a replacement link
  removes the stale credential; legacy local verified flags grant nothing. Expired-session reads
  clear displayed content and return to contact verification. All four CORS profiles allow the header.
- V117 adds the nullable hash without manufacturing credentials for historical rows, revokes all
  existing sessions, revokes inserts from old writers without a hash, requires expiry for every
  credential-bearing session, prevents duplicate hashes, and freezes recipient/link/hash identity.
  Historical session IDs and provenance remain. Existing direct-grant ShareLinks are unchanged.
  Rolling compatibility is fail-closed: an old writer may insert a row but it is revoked and cannot
  become content-capable. Deploy the new client/server together; old sessions require fresh proof.
  Feature disablement needs no destructive schema rollback and cannot restore token-only authority.

  `AddInformationRequestGroupOccurrenceCommand.parentOccurrenceId` is wired through

  frontend `CreateInformationRequestGroupOccurrenceRequest`. Phase 5's own tests-to-write-first list
  names "Two nested occurrences with independent Field ... paths", which did not exist. Four tests
  were added to `InformationRequestGroupOccurrenceServiceTest`: a nested occurrence roots its path
  at its parent (`items[0]/entries[0]`) and provisions its own Field Value Set; adding a parent
  occurrence materializes the nested group's authored minimum beneath it; two nested occurrences
  under different parents keep independent paths, requirement rows, and Value Sets; and the parent
  reference is validated in both directions (a root group naming a parent, and a nested group naming
  none, both refuse with `GROUP_OCCURRENCE_PARENT_INVALID` without advancing the response revision).
  All four passed on first run against the existing production code, so the defect was missing
  coverage rather than missing behavior, and no production Kotlin changed.
- Open gap, needs a scoping decision before Phase 5 can close: condition evaluation is not
  occurrence-aware, and the consequence is silent loss of owed work rather than a visible refusal.
  Verified in source, not inferred:
  1. `InformationRequestConditionEvaluationService.currentFieldValues` resolves values from
     `fieldValueSetRepository.findRoot(assignment.id)` only, so a Field predicate reading a Field
     collected by an occurrence-anchored Requirement finds no value and evaluates UNKNOWN forever.
  2. `currentDispositions` keys by Requirement key, but an occurrence-anchored Requirement has one
     runtime row per occurrence sharing that key, and `.toMap()` collapses them, so an arbitrary
     occurrence wins by repository order. That is non-deterministic, which the Phase 5 exit criteria
     forbid outright.
  3. `evaluate` returns one state per rule key and `InformationRequestDto.conditionEvaluations`
     projects one state per rule key, so per-occurrence truth cannot be expressed even with correct
     inputs.
  4. `InformationRequestTemplateConfigurationValidator.validateConditions` only checks that a
     predicate's Field is collected by some Requirement in the Version. It does not refuse a
     predicate whose source Requirement is occurrence-anchored, so the unsupported shape is
     authorable today.
  5. `InformationRequestCompletenessProgressService.contributionFor` treats any CONDITIONAL
     Requirement whose rule state is not TRUE as HIDDEN, and HIDDEN contributes to neither the
     numerator nor the denominator. An UNKNOWN rule therefore removes the Requirement from progress
     entirely, so a request can report 100 percent complete while a conditional Requirement inside a
     repeatable group was never shown or collected.
  6. The UNKNOWN-is-hidden rule is deliberate and pinned:
     `InformationRequestCompletenessProgressServiceTest` authors both a `when-answer-not-needed`
     FALSE case and a `when-answer-unknown` UNKNOWN case and asserts both are HIDDEN with a
     denominator of 4. Changing it is a reversal of a recorded `P5-T7` decision, not a bug fix, so
     it was not changed unilaterally.
  7. The `multi_party_staged_evidence_request` stress fixture already authors this exact shape: its
     conditional Requirement carries `occurrenceAnchorKey = "reported-item"` while its rule
     `when-subject-is-active` reads `sourceRequirementKey = "delegate-note"`.

### 2026-09-08: `P5-T7` deterministic structured-response progress

- Current phase and task: Phase 5, Structured Responses, Repeatable Groups, and Conditions. `P5-T7`
  is complete.
- Status at session end: added `InformationRequestCompletenessProgressService`, a service-level
  progress evaluator for the current structured-response slice. It loads the runtime request,
  runtime Requirements, Template bindings, active draft responses, and current condition
  evaluations, then applies one deterministic formula. Required Requirements and condition-true
  conditional Requirements enter the denominator. Optional unanswered Requirements and conditional
  Requirements whose rule is false, unknown, or not evaluable are excluded as non-owed or hidden.
  A structured answer is complete when the active response has a Field Value Set or any disposition
  other than `NOT_ANSWERED`, so `WAIVED`, `PARTIALLY_PROVIDED`, `NOT_APPLICABLE`, `UNAVAILABLE`,
  `EXCEPTION_REQUESTED`, and `SATISFIED_BY_REFERENCE` all satisfy the structured-response slice
  once the existing disposition and narrative rules have accepted them. Rejected outcomes are
  represented through `InformationRequestCompletenessContributionEvaluator` extension
  contributions and count incomplete in the denominator. Extension contributions replace the
  structured contribution for the same Requirement ID, preventing later evidence or review logic
  from double-counting one Requirement.
- Tests added first: added
  `InformationRequestCompletenessProgressServiceTest.required optional hidden waived and rejected
  structured responses have deterministic denominators`, covering required provided, optional
  unanswered, condition-true unanswered, condition-false hidden, condition-unknown hidden, waived,
  and rejected extension contribution cases.

  evaluation projection exposed on a runtime request) remain.

  already normalized and validated an authored `conditionRules` document (rule key uniqueness,

  conditional requirements) and `InformationRequestConditionEvaluator` already evaluated a rule

  every other part of a Template Version configuration already has (sections, bindings, groups):
  `InformationRequestTemplateConditionRule` (rule key, expression version) and

  `InformationRequestTemplateConditionPredicateLiteral`, the same way `FieldValueSelection` holds a
  Field answer's own selected codes rather than an array column. The scalar/list literal conversion
  between the canonical JSON a predicate is authored and read as and the typed storage columns is a
  new, independently unit-tested object, `InformationRequestConditionPredicateLiteralCodec`, used by

### 2026-09-07: `P5-T2c` runtime group occurrence commands added

- Current phase and task: Phase 5, Structured Responses, Repeatable Groups, and Conditions. `P5-T2c`
  was the active task and is complete. `P5-T2a`, `P5-T2b`, and `P5-T2c` are all complete, so `P5-T2`
  is complete.
- Status at session end: authenticated and no-auth callers can add, remove, and reorder repeatable
  group occurrences at runtime through a shared application service. The service uses the same
  response-mutation lifecycle gate as response drafts, requires the frozen execution grant to remain
  usable for continuation, enforces central `INFORMATION_REQUEST_REQUIREMENT_RESPOND` authorization
  against the Information Request aggregate, validates `If-Match` against the request response ETag,
  scopes replay through Command Receipts, and records a `SAVE_RESPONSE` transition with
  `GROUP_OCCURRENCES_CHANGED`. Adding an occurrence allocates a stable path from all siblings
  including removed ones, creates occurrence Field Value Sets when the request has a Schema
  assignment, creates runtime Requirements and current revisions for bindings anchored to the group,
  and recursively provisions each child group's authored minimum occurrences. Removing an occurrence
  marks it and its descendants removed with canonical principal provenance while retaining existing
  occurrences, Requirements, revisions, and responses for addressability. Reordering changes only
  active siblings' `occurrenceIndex`; `occurrencePath` is never rewritten.
