### 2026-09-07: `P5-T2b` runtime group occurrence instances added

- Current phase and task: Phase 5, Structured Responses, Repeatable Groups, and Conditions. `P5-T2`
  is split into `P5-T2a` (template-level definitions, complete), `P5-T2b` (runtime occurrence
  instances, this session, complete), and `P5-T2c` (runtime add/remove/reorder, next).
- Status at session end: `P5-T2a` left two open questions: where an occurrence `FieldValueSet`
  get-or-create belongs, and how issuance materializes a group's first runtime occurrence(s). Both
  are resolved. A new `InformationRequestGroupOccurrence` entity (migration `V112`) records one
  runtime repetition of a template group against one request: a stable `occurrencePath`, an
  `occurrenceIndex` among its siblings, and a `parentOccurrenceId` that nests a child group's
  occurrences inside their parent occurrence, mirroring the template's own group nesting.
  `InformationRequestTemplateMaterializer.materialize` now loads the version's groups, walks the
  group tree parent-first, and creates exactly `minOccurrences` occurrences for each group -- zero
  where a group is authored with none, which is deliberate: a group's first occurrence exists only
  where its own cardinality asked for one, matching how `SchemaAssignmentService` already treats a
  repetition ("a repetition is not created on demand, because a repetition exists only where
  something added it"). A binding's occurrence anchor key now resolves to that group's occurrence
  paths and materializes one `InformationRequestRequirement` per occurrence (still exactly one at
  `"root"` for a binding with no anchor, preserving every existing test's expectations); an anchor
  whose group currently has no occurrences materializes nothing for that binding, to be filled in by
  `P5-T2c`. `SchemaAssignmentService` gained `createOccurrenceValueSet`, a small public get-or-create
  that mirrors `createRootValueSet` but is never invoked implicitly by a write -- only the
  materializer (and, later, `P5-T2c`'s runtime add) calls it, immediately after saving each new group
  occurrence, and only when the request already carries Field requirements (the same
  `hasFieldRequirements` flag that already gates the Schema assignment itself). This closes the
  `valueSetForWrite` throw for a missing occurrence set: a Field Requirement anchored to a group
  occurrence can now be answered as soon as that occurrence is materialized.
- Tests added first: `SchemaAssignmentService.createOccurrenceValueSet` was added to
  `RootFieldValueSetTest` with three cases (creates the set when missing, is idempotent when one
  already exists for the path, refuses when the resource carries no Schema Assignment at all) before
  being wired into the materializer. `InformationRequestTemplateMaterializerTest` gained five cases:
  one Requirement per group occurrence at that occurrence's path; a nested group's occurrences
  materialized under each of its parent's occurrences with the correct parent-prefixed path and
  `parentOccurrenceId`; a group with `minOccurrences = 0` materializing no occurrences and no
  Requirement for its anchored binding; a Field-bearing request provisioning each new occurrence's
  Field Value Set; and a non-Field-bearing request never calling `createOccurrenceValueSet`.

- Decisions made: an occurrence's stable path is `"<groupKey>[<index>]"`, with a nested occurrence's
  path prefixed by its parent occurrence's own path and a `/` (for example
  `"items[0]/entries[1]"`); this keeps every path distinct from the literal `"root"` used for a
  non-repeating binding regardless of what a group is named. A group starts with exactly its
  authored `minOccurrences`, including zero, rather than always materializing at least one: the
  cardinality is what the Template author already asked for, and forcing a first occurrence past a
  zero minimum would silently create process data nobody configured. `createOccurrenceValueSet` is a
  plain get-or-create with no access-context parameter, unlike every other public
  `SchemaAssignmentService` write: it is only ever called from server-side provisioning that already
  ran its own authorization (schema assignment, and later `P5-T2c`'s own runtime add), never directly
  from a caller-supplied command.

  carrying no database-level foreign key.

  current response on the request (`responseStore.findCurrentForRequest`), which is safe for an
  internal caller with full-request visibility but would leak a co-party's disposition/narrative to a
  single-occurrence respondent if echoed verbatim; the two new resources filter
  `result.responses` down to the requirement ids the incoming patch actually named before mapping to
  DTOs. This closes, for the response surface introduced here, the Phase 4 exit criterion

### 2026-09-07: `P4-T9` complete: minimal authenticated and no-auth runtime request read shell (detail, parties, no-auth token resolution)

- Current phase and task: Phase 4, Authorization and Dual Access Surfaces. `P4-T9` (add the minimal
  authenticated and no-auth request shell that proves safe request list and detail projection, token
  handling, and equal capability discovery for the walking scenarios).
- Status at session end: `P4-T9` is complete. Owner-facing detail projection, owner- and
  party-facing party projection, and the no-auth respondent read counterpart for both are now all
  reachable from REST, reusing the exact same application services on both surfaces so they cannot
  diverge:
  - `InformationRequestQueryService.findById` (new): request-scoped `INFORMATION_REQUEST_VIEW`
    authorization plus the existing owner entitlement gate, mirroring `listForExchange`'s pattern but
    at `ResourceRef.informationRequest(requestId)` instead of the exchange.
  - `InformationRequestResource.get` (`GET /information-requests/{id}`, new): authenticated detail,
    delegating to `findById`.
  - `InformationRequestPartyResource` (new, `GET /information-requests/{id}/parties`): the first REST
    caller of `InformationRequestPartyQueryService.listForRequest` (built in `P4-T6a`, unreachable from
    any surface until now).
  - `InformationRequestNoAuthReadAccessService` (new): turns a presented bootstrap
    `X-Request-Access-Token` into the same `RequestAccessContext` shape the authenticated surface
    builds, by resolving the link (`InformationRequestContactProofService.resolveBootstrapLink`, made
    public and reused rather than duplicated), finding its usable session
    (`RequestAccessSessionService.findUsableForShareLink`, new), and building the context through
    `InformationRequestAccessContextFactory.fromBootstrapSession` (built in `P4-T4`, unreachable from
    any surface until now) -- the first production caller of both. Refuses with the new
    `ACCESS_SESSION_REQUIRED` catalog code when the link is otherwise valid but no session has ever
    been verified for it, and touches the session's use count on every successful resolution, so the
    same token stays reusable across many reads without repeating contact proof.
  - `InformationRequestNoAuthRequestResource` (new, `no-auth/information-requests/{id}` and
    `.../parties`): mirrors the authenticated resource's two reads, delegating to the identical
    `InformationRequestQueryService`/`InformationRequestPartyQueryService` calls after resolving the
    token and confirming the resolved session's request id matches the one named in the path (refusing
    a token used to read a different request's path with 404 rather than trusting the path blindly).
    Already covered by the existing `/no-auth/information-requests/` allowlist prefix in
    `EndpointAuthorizationFilter`, confirmed by a new parity test rather than assumed.

### 2026-09-06: `P4-T7b` complete: idempotent `RequestExecutionUsageReservation` capacity ledger

- Current phase and task: Phase 4, Authorization and Dual Access Surfaces. `P4-T7` (Resolve
  subscription checks from the owning Exchange and freeze execution entitlement/quota at issuance),
  subtask `P4-T7b` (the idempotent `RequestExecutionUsageReservation` model: reserve, consume,
  release, and roll back capacity against a `RequestExecutionGrant` under concurrent operations).
- Status at session end: `P4-T7a`'s `RequestExecutionGrant` freezes an `additionalRecipientCap` but
  nothing tracked how much of it was actually spent, so a second respondent could always be added
  right up to (and past, under a race) the frozen limit. Added `RequestExecutionUsageReservation`
  (migration `V109`, table `request_execution_usage_reservation`, one row per logical reservation
  keyed by `(grant_id, usage_kind, reservation_key)`) and
  `InformationRequestExecutionUsageReservationService` with four operations: `reserve` (idempotent by
  `reservationKey`, locks the parent grant row with `findByIdForUpdate` before summing active usage
  and comparing against the grant's cap for that `RequestExecutionUsageKind`, so two callers racing
  for the last unit of capacity are serialized rather than both succeeding), `consume` (finalizes a
  `RESERVED` row to `CONSUMED`; both statuses count as active usage, so consuming does not change the
  ledger total), `release` (frees a `RESERVED` row's capacity before it was finalized), and `rollback`
  (frees a `CONSUMED` row's capacity after the fact, for usage undone later, e.g. a party removed).
  All four are idempotent on repeat calls in their own terminal/no-op state and refuse any other
  cross-state transition (e.g. `release` on an already-`CONSUMED` row, `rollback` on a still-`RESERVED`
  row) with `IllegalStateException`. Added `RequestExecutionUsageKind` (currently only
  `ADDITIONAL_RECIPIENT`, matching the only cap the grant carries today) and
  `RequestExecutionUsageReservationStatus` (`RESERVED`/`CONSUMED`/`RELEASED`/`ROLLED_BACK`) as their
  own enum files alongside the existing single-enum-per-file convention. Nothing yet calls `reserve`
  from request-party or Field-write code paths; that wiring is `P4-T7c`'s job, once continuation-path
  checks are redirected to the frozen grant.
- Tests added first: `InformationRequestExecutionUsageReservationServiceTest.kt` (10 cases, mocked
  repositories): reserving within the cap creates a `RESERVED` row; reserving past the cap throws
  `RequestExecutionUsageExhaustedException` carrying the grant id, cap, active usage, and requested
  quantity, and never calls `save`; an uncapped grant (`additionalRecipientCap == null`) never calls
  `sumActiveQuantity` and always succeeds; reserving twice with the same key returns the original row
  unchanged without re-locking the grant or re-checking capacity; consume/release/rollback each have a
  happy-path-then-idempotent-repeat case and a cross-state-refusal case (released cannot be consumed,
  reserved cannot be rolled back directly, consumed cannot be released).
  `RequestExecutionUsageReservationConcurrencyPostgresContractTest.kt` (2 cases, real Postgres via
  Testcontainers plus Flyway, mirroring `OrganizationSeatConcurrencyPostgresContractTest`'s raw-JDBC
  `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` pattern rather than the mocked service, since only a real database can prove
  the lock actually serializes concurrent transactions): four concurrent callers racing to reserve one
  unit each against a two-unit cap must see exactly two accepted and two refused, with the ledger
  settling at exactly `2`; releasing a reservation frees its capacity for a later caller to reuse.
- Failure observed before implementation: Ran the mocked service tests against a `reserve` that always
  inserted without checking `sumActiveQuantity`; the exhaustion case failed with "Expected
  RequestExecutionUsageExhaustedException to be thrown, but nothing was thrown" and the never-`save`
  verification failed. Ran the cross-state-refusal cases against a `consume`/`release`/`rollback` that
  unconditionally transitioned regardless of current status; each failed with "expected:
  <IllegalStateException> to be thrown" once the guard `when` branches were temporarily removed.
- Implementation completed: as described above. Restored the capacity check in `reserve` and the
  `when`-based status guards in `consume`/`release`/`rollback` and reran; all 10 cases passed.
- Files changed: `RequestExecutionUsageKind.kt` (new),
  `RequestExecutionUsageReservationStatus.kt` (new), `RequestExecutionUsageReservation.kt` (new
  entity), `RequestExecutionUsageReservationRepository.kt` (new),
  `RequestExecutionUsageExhaustedException.kt` (new),
  `InformationRequestExecutionUsageReservationService.kt` (new),
  `InformationRequestExecutionUsageReservationServiceTest.kt` (new),
  `RequestExecutionUsageReservationConcurrencyPostgresContractTest.kt` (new).
- Database migrations added: `V109__request_execution_usage_reservation.sql` (table
  `request_execution_usage_reservation`, a unique constraint on `(grant_id, usage_kind,
  reservation_key)` for idempotency, and check constraints mirroring the grant table's own style).
- Focused tests run and results: `InformationRequestExecutionUsageReservationServiceTest` -- 10 tests,
  0 failures (4 of 10 failed before the fix, for the intended reasons above), via
  `./mvnw -o test -Dtest=com.docuhyphen.app.api.service.informationrequest.InformationRequestExecutionUsageReservationServiceTest`.
  `RequestExecutionUsageReservationConcurrencyPostgresContractTest` could not run in this session's
  environment: `Could not find a valid Docker environment`, the identical failure mode produced by the

  -- 448 tests, 0 failures, 4 pre-existing Docker/Kafka environment errors (unchanged known baseline,
  unrelated to this change), 16 skipped.
- Help documentation reviewed or updated: Not applicable; this is a service-layer capacity ledger with
  no REST surface, UI, or other user-visible behavior yet. `web-app/` untouched, `npx tsc --noEmit` not
  run.
- Decisions made: Modeled `reserve`/`consume`/`release`/`rollback` as four distinct verbs rather than a
  single mutable "amount used" counter, so that a later caller (`P4-T7c`) can attach one reservation
  row per concrete unit of work (one party, one upload) and reverse exactly that unit later without
  recomputing everyone else's share. Chose a caller-supplied `reservationKey` (rather than, say,
  requiring the caller to look up an existing reservation first) so the same idempotency pattern
  `InformationRequestExecutionGrantService.issueGrant` already uses for the grant itself extends
  naturally to each individual reservation. Locked the grant row (not a separate counter row) for
  `reserve`, reusing the exact `findByIdForUpdate` pattern `OrganizationSeatGuard` already uses to
  serialize seat activation, rather than inventing a new locking primitive. Scoped
  `RequestExecutionUsageKind` to just `ADDITIONAL_RECIPIENT` since that is the only cap
  `RequestExecutionGrant` carries today; upload and storage kinds are deliberately not stubbed in since
  nothing sizes them yet. Did not wire `reserve`/`consume`/`release`/`rollback` into any caller
  (request-party assignment, Field writes): that redirection, plus proving a lapsed owner's respondent
  can still work within reserved limits, is explicitly `P4-T7c`'s scope, not this one's.
- Assumptions: A `reservationKey` is unique per logical unit of work within one grant and one usage
  kind (e.g. the party id being added), chosen by the future caller in `P4-T7c`; this session does not
  define what that caller passes since no caller exists yet. `consume` and `release` both only accept
  a `RESERVED` source state; `rollback` only accepts `CONSUMED`, so undoing a still-provisional
  reservation goes through `release`, never `rollback`, keeping the two verbs non-overlapping.

### 2026-09-06: `P4-T7a` complete: `RequestExecutionGrant` freezes commercial position at issuance

- Current phase and task: Phase 4, Authorization and Dual Access Surfaces. `P4-T7` (Resolve
  subscription checks from the owning Exchange and freeze execution entitlement/quota at issuance).
  This task is too large for one session, so it is split into `P4-T7a` through `P4-T7d`; this session
  completed `P4-T7a` only, the frozen grant record itself with nothing yet consuming it.
- Status at session end: `InformationRequestEntitlementGuard` already resolved subscription checks
  (`PlanFeature.INFORMATION_REQUESTS`) from the parent Exchange's owner, but every call re-reads the
  live subscription, so a paid lapse or trial expiry after issuance would strand an in-flight request's
  respondents and reviewers -- the exact defect `P4-T7` exists to fix. Added `RequestExecutionGrant`
  (migration `V108`, table `request_execution_grant`, one row per request via a unique `request_id`)
  and `InformationRequestExecutionGrantService.issueGrant(request, exchange)`, wired into
  `InformationRequestLifecycleService.issue()`. It snapshots owner type/id, `planCode`,
  `subscriptionStatus`, the enforcement mode observed, a `trialExpiresAt` when the owner is trialing, a
  `mutationAllowanceExpiresAt` (trial end, grace-period end while `PAST_DUE`, or paid-through date while
  `CANCELED`, else none), and `additionalRecipientCap` from `PlanLimits.maxAdditionalParticipantsPerExchange`.

  yet reads this grant back; it is inert until `P4-T7c`.

  plan freezes owner/plan/enforcement mode with no trial expiry; a trialing personal plan freezes the
  trial end as the mutation allowance; a past-due organization plan freezes the grace-period end as the
  mutation allowance; issuing twice for the same request returns the original grant and never calls
  `resolve`/`save` again; an Exchange with neither owner set cannot be granted.
  `InformationRequestLifecycleServiceTest.kt` gained one case: issuing a request calls
  `executionGrantService.issueGrant(request, exchange)` with the exact locked Exchange.

### 2026-09-06: `P4-T6a` complete: recipient-safe party projection proves and closes a concrete cross-party identity leak

- Current phase and task: Phase 4, Authorization and Dual Access Surfaces. `P4-T6` (Apply
  recipient-safe projection to every read and mutation response). No party, occurrence, or response
  DTO or read resource existed anywhere in the repository before this session, so the first slice
  (`P4-T6a`) adds the projection for the one entity that already carries audience-sensitive
  identifying data today, `InformationRequestParty`. `InformationRequestRequirement`/
  `InformationRequestRequirementRevision` (the runtime occurrence) carry only template/source
  references and a path string, no principal-identifying field, so there is nothing to redact there
  yet; response and evidence content does not exist until Phase 5-7. Those are tracked below as
  `P4-T6b`, not attempted early.
- Status at session end: The concrete gap: every `InformationRequestShareRoleKey`
  (`SUBJECT`/`CONTRIBUTOR`/`PREPARER`/`ATTESTOR`/`REVIEWER`/`DECISION_MAKER`) is granted
  `Capability.INFORMATION_REQUEST_READ` (`RoleCapabilities.kt`), so `Action.INFORMATION_REQUEST_VIEW`
  alone cannot decide which party rows a caller should see in full -- any active party on a request
  passes that same check. Only `DECISION_MAKER` additionally holds `Capability.INFORMATION_REQUEST_ADMIN`,
  which resolves to `Action.INFORMATION_REQUEST_MANAGE_PARTIES`. Added `InformationRequestPartyDto`
  (`model/dto/InformationRequestPartyDtos.kt`) and `InformationRequestPartyDtoMapper`
  (`model/InformationRequestPartyDtoMapper.kt`) with a `revealIdentity: Boolean` parameter that nulls
  `principalId`, `principalKind`, `subjectIdentityRefId`, and `exchangeRecipientId` when false, and
  `InformationRequestPartyQueryService.listForRequest` (new,
  `service/informationrequest/InformationRequestPartyQueryService.kt`), which loads a request's active
  parties, requires `INFORMATION_REQUEST_VIEW` on the request, separately asks
  `INFORMATION_REQUEST_MANAGE_PARTIES` to decide `isManager`, and reveals a party row's identity only
  when the caller is a manager or the row is the caller's own party (`principalKind`/`principalId`
  match against `access.principal`). This is service-layer only; it is unreachable from any REST
  surface until a party resource is added (planned for `P4-T9`, per the existing phase ordering, which
  places the actual request/party read shell after `P4-T6`-`P4-T8`).
- Tests added first: `InformationRequestPartyQueryServiceTest.kt` (4 cases): a non-managing peer sees
  their own party row in full but the other active party's `principalId`/`principalKind`/
  `exchangeRecipientId`/`subjectIdentityRefId` redacted to null; a manager (`INFORMATION_REQUEST_MANAGE_PARTIES`
  granted) sees every party's identity in full; a caller denied `INFORMATION_REQUEST_VIEW` never
  reaches the party repository; a missing request is refused before authorization.
- Failure observed before implementation: Wrote the DTO, a mapper that ignored its `revealIdentity`
  parameter and always mapped every identifying field, and a query service that unconditionally passed
  `revealIdentity = true` (deliberately not yet gating on manager status or row ownership), so the
  file compiled. Ran the new test: the peer-redaction case failed with
  `expected: <null> but was: <the peer's actual principalId>`, i.e. the party list, if such a resource
  existed today, would disclose one party's principal identity to any other unrelated party on the
  same request purely because both share `INFORMATION_REQUEST_READ`. Confirmed via
  `./mvnw -o test -Dtest=com.docuhyphen.app.api.service.informationrequest.InformationRequestPartyQueryServiceTest`.
- Implementation completed: Made the mapper honor `revealIdentity` (`.takeIf { revealIdentity }` on
  each identity field) and made the query service compute `isManager` from the
  `INFORMATION_REQUEST_MANAGE_PARTIES` decision and `revealIdentity = isManager || isOwnParty(...)`
  per row, where `isOwnParty` compares `principalKind`/`principalId` against `access.principal`.
- Files changed: `InformationRequestPartyDtos.kt` (new), `InformationRequestPartyDtoMapper.kt` (new),
  `InformationRequestPartyQueryService.kt` (new), `InformationRequestPartyQueryServiceTest.kt` (new).
  No entity, resource, or migration changed.
- Database migrations added: None.
- Focused tests run and results: `InformationRequestPartyQueryServiceTest` -- 4 tests, 0 failures
  (after the fix; 1 of 4 failed before, for the intended reason above).
- Full validation commands and results: `./mvnw -o test-compile` -- full project compiles.
  `./mvnw -o test -Dtest="com.docuhyphen.app.api.service.auth.authz.**,com.docuhyphen.app.api.**.informationrequest.**"`
  -- 436 tests (432 baseline plus these 4 new cases), 0 failures, 4 pre-existing Docker/Kafka
  environment errors (unchanged known baseline, unrelated to this change), 16 skipped.
- Help documentation reviewed or updated: Not applicable. Nothing added here is reachable from any
  REST surface or UI yet (no party resource exists), so there is no user-visible behavior to document.

- Decisions made: Put the redaction decision inside the query service rather than in a REST layer, so

### 2026-09-06: `P4-T4` fifth slice: verified-registration upgrade path (`ParticipantAccountLink`)

- Current phase and task: Phase 4, Authorization and Dual Access Surfaces. This session implemented
  the last remaining slice of `P4-T4`: the verified-registration upgrade path that lets a respondent
  who has been acting as an email-only Participant complete registration as a full App User without
  losing or rewriting their prior access history.
- Status at session end: `P4-T4` is now functionally complete at the service layer (still unreachable
  from any REST surface, which is `P4-T5`). Added a new `InformationRequestParticipantAccountUpgradeService`
  with a single `upgrade(command)` operation. Unlike `rotate`/`replace`/`revoke` on
  `InformationRequestBootstrapShareLinkService` (which authorize via `INFORMATION_REQUEST_MANAGE_PARTIES`,
  i.e. an admin acting on someone else's link), this operation authenticates the caller by their own
  active `RequestAccessSession` (via a new `RequestAccessSessionService.requireActive(sessionId)`),
  since the actor here is the respondent themself completing their own upgrade, not a party manager.
  The operation: (1) resolves the session's bootstrap `ShareLink` and the request party bound to its
  Share, confirming the party is still `PARTICIPANT`-held and the session's participant principal
  matches it; (2) loads the caller-supplied `appUserId` via `AppUserService.getById` (never creating an
  account -- the explicit anti-goal from the task text) and refuses the upgrade unless that App User's
  email matches the Participant's verified `emailLower` exactly
  (`PARTICIPANT_ACCOUNT_EMAIL_MISMATCH`); (3) persists a new `ParticipantAccountLink` row
  (`participant_id` unique, `app_user_id`, plus `linked_via_information_request_id`/
  `linked_via_share_link_id` provenance) via a new `ParticipantAccountLinkRepository`, or reuses an
  existing one for the same participant when this is a second Information Request upgrading the same
  identity, refusing outright when an existing link already names a *different* App User
  (`PARTICIPANT_ACCOUNT_ALREADY_LINKED`, the identity-collision case); (4) grants the App User an
  equivalent Share on the same Information Request/role via
  `ShareService.grantRoleKeyWithPrincipalProvenance` -- a brand new Share row, since the Participant's
  original Share, party, and ShareLink rows are never touched or revoked, preserving history exactly as
  the task text requires; (5) revokes every still-active bootstrap-mode ShareLink bound to that Share
  (a new `ShareLinkRepository.findActiveBootstrapLinksForShare`, covering rotation/replacement lineage,
  not just the one link the session came from) plus every session minted from each, reusing
  `RequestAccessSessionService.revokeAllForShareLink`. Uses Command Receipts
  (`CommandActorRef.accessSession(sessionId)` as the actor, matching the session-authenticated shape;
  a replay safely re-derives the same link and Share rather than erroring, since no secret is at stake)
  and the party's `partyRevision` as the expected-revision precondition, matching the other `P4-T4`
  slices.
- Tests added first: New `InformationRequestParticipantAccountUpgradeServiceTest.kt` (12 cases): the
  success path (equivalent User Share granted, original party untouched), ParticipantAccountLink
  persistence, bootstrap ShareLink/session revocation, a proof that `AppUserService` is touched only
  through `getById` (no temporary-account creation), a proof that `ShareService.revokeWithPrincipalProvenance`
  is never called (unchanged historical provenance), email-mismatch denial, already-linked-to-a-different-account
  denial, a second-request reuse-of-existing-link case, revoked-session denial, non-Participant-party
  denial, precondition enforcement, and idempotent replay. Also added 4 new focused cases to
  `RequestAccessSessionServiceTest.kt` for the new `requireActive` method (active, not-found, revoked,
  expired).

### 2026-09-06: `P4-T4` fourth slice: bootstrap ShareLink rotation, replacement, and revocation

- Current phase and task: Phase 4, Authorization and Dual Access Surfaces. `P4-T4` remains open. This
  session built on the prior three slices (`ShareLinkMode` plus central-authorizer refusal, persisted
  `RequestAccessSession` plus bootstrap issuance, and recipient contact-proof verification) and added
  the generic rotate/replace/revoke capability the task text calls for, so a future session can wire
  `P3-T11b` (ShareLink bootstrap rotation on reassignment) and `P3-T11c` (RequestAccessSession
  revocation on reassignment) to it without building the underlying mechanism itself.
- Status at session end: `InformationRequestBootstrapShareLinkService` gained three operations,
  each following the same Command Receipt pattern as `issue` and reusing the acting party's
  `partyRevision` as the expected-revision precondition (via `InformationRequestETag.partyOf`),
  since `ShareLink` itself carries no revision counter of its own:
  - `rotate(RotateInformationRequestBootstrapShareLinkCommand)`: replaces the link's secret in
    place (same row and id), resets `usedCount` to 0, clears any outstanding
    `contactOtpHash`/`contactOtpExpiresAt` challenge, and records `rotatedAt`/`rotationCount`. A
    replay under the same idempotency key cannot recover the new secret, so it throws
    `ACCESS_LINK_ALREADY_ROTATED` (mirroring `issue`'s `ACCESS_LINK_ALREADY_ISSUED` behavior)
    rather than returning the stale response.
  - `replace(ReplaceInformationRequestBootstrapShareLinkCommand)`: revokes the old link and issues a
    brand new one bound to the same request-party Share, with its own `expiresAt`/`maxUses` and
    `replacesShareLinkId` pointing back at the link it replaced. A replay throws
    `ACCESS_LINK_ALREADY_REPLACED` for the same reason as rotate.
  - `revoke(RevokeInformationRequestBootstrapShareLinkCommand)`: marks the link revoked and is
    idempotent on an already-revoked link (no secret is at stake, so a replay safely re-reads the
    current row via `shareLinkRepository.findById` instead of throwing).
  All three refuse a link that is not `VERIFICATION_BOOTSTRAP` mode (`IllegalArgumentException`,
  preserving direct-grant ShareLinks untouched), refuse an already-revoked or expired link before
  rotating or replacing it (`ACCESS_LINK_REVOKED`/`ACCESS_LINK_EXPIRED`), and lock the row with
  `findByIdForUpdate` before mutating it. All three call the new
  `RequestAccessSessionService.revokeAllForShareLink(shareLinkId)` (backed by a new
  `RequestAccessSessionRepository.findActiveByShareLinkId` query) so every still-active session
  minted from the affected link is revoked whenever its link is rotated, replaced, or revoked --
  a credential change on the link can never leave a previously minted session usable.
- Tests added first: Extended `InformationRequestBootstrapShareLinkServiceTest.kt` with 10 new cases:
  rotation mints a new token/resets use count/clears a stale challenge and revokes existing sessions;
  rotating a revoked, expired, or direct-grant link is refused; rotation is denied without
  manage-parties capability; rotation requires the current party ETag; a repeated rotation cannot
  recover the new token; replacement revokes the old link and binds the new one via
  `replacesShareLinkId`; replacing a revoked link is refused; a repeated replacement cannot recover
  the new token; revocation marks the link revoked and revokes its sessions; revoking an
  already-revoked link is a no-op; revocation is denied without manage-parties capability.
- Failure observed before implementation: Compilation failure (unresolved references to the
  not-yet-existing `rotate`/`replace`/`revoke` methods, their command classes,
  `RequestAccessSessionService.revokeAllForShareLink`, and the new
  `ACCESS_LINK_ALREADY_ROTATED`/`ACCESS_LINK_ALREADY_REPLACED` catalog codes) in the extended test
  file.

### 2026-09-06: `P4-T4` third slice: recipient contact-proof verification service

- Current phase and task: Phase 4, Authorization and Dual Access Surfaces. `P4-T4` remains open. This
  session built on the prior two slices (`ShareLinkMode` plus central-authorizer refusal, and the
  persisted `RequestAccessSession`/bootstrap issuance service) and added the contact-proof

- Status at session end: New `InformationRequestContactProofService` with `issueChallenge(rawToken)`
  and `verifyChallenge(rawToken, otp, sessionExpiresAt)`. `issueChallenge` hashes the presented token,
  resolves the bootstrap-mode `ShareLink` (rejecting an unknown token, a `DIRECT_GRANT` link, a
  revoked, expired, or usage-exhausted link, or a link no longer bound to an active
  `InformationRequestParty`), resolves that party's contact email (`ExternalParticipantRepository`
  for a `PARTICIPANT` principal, `AppUserService` for a `USER` principal), generates a one-time code
  via the existing `OtpService`, stores only its hash and an explicit expiry on the `ShareLink` itself
  (`contactOtpHash`/`contactOtpExpiresAt`, migration `V105`), and emails it. `verifyChallenge` re-runs
  the same link resolution, checks the stored hash and expiry, clears both on success (single-use),
  and calls `RequestAccessSessionService.issue` with a `PrincipalRef` built from the party's own
  `principalKind`/`principalId`, returning the minted `RequestAccessSession`.

  code all refused without minting a session; and USER-kind party contact resolution through

  with no request-party Share yet, for a revoked party, when the caller lacks
  `INFORMATION_REQUEST_MANAGE_PARTIES`, and when the supplied precondition does not match the party's
  current ETag. Issuance is wrapped in `CommandReceiptService.runOnce` for idempotency; because the raw
  token is never persisted (only its SHA-256 hash), a replayed retry cannot resurrect the original
  secret, so a replay throws a new stable code (`INFORMATION_REQUEST_ACCESS_LINK_ALREADY_ISSUED`)
  rather than silently minting a second active link or fabricating a fake response -- this is a
  deliberate decision, not an oversight; see below.

  binding/participant/verification-strength/expiry; issuing against a `DIRECT_GRANT` link is refused;

  `ShareLink` with a bootstrap mode, add persisted `RequestAccessSession`, requireRecipientSignIn
  refusal, contact-proof issuance, verified registration upgrade, Command Receipts). This session
  implemented only its first, independently-testable slice: the `ShareLinkMode` field itself and the
  central authorizer's refusal to ever resolve a bootstrap-mode link as a content grant. `P4-T4`
  remains open; the rest of its scope (persisted `RequestAccessSession`, issuance/rotation/revocation
  services, `requireRecipientSignIn` refusal, contact-proof verification, registration upgrade,
  `ParticipantAccountLink`, Command Receipts) is unstarted.

  column on `ShareLink`, defaulting existing rows and all existing callers to `DIRECT_GRANT` so
  current direct-grant ShareLink behavior is unchanged. Taught
  `DefaultAuthorizationService.resolveLinkGrant` (the PUBLIC_LINK grant path consulted whenever
  `AuthorizationContext.shareLinkTokenHash` is present) to return no grant at all when the resolved
  `ShareLink.linkMode` is `VERIFICATION_BOOTSTRAP`, before any status, expiry, use-count, or MFA check
  runs. This is the exact "make the central authorizer refuse to turn a bootstrap-mode link into a
  content grant" sentence from the `P4-T4` task text, made concrete and independently testable ahead
  of the session/issuance work that will actually create bootstrap-mode links.

  touched: it already requires `share.resourceType == EXCHANGE`, and a bootstrap-mode link's covering
  Share will be a request-party Share (not `EXCHANGE`), so that path already structurally excludes it
  once issuance exists; no redundant check was added there.

  otherwise-valid, active, covering ShareLink/Share pair, sets `linkMode = VERIFICATION_BOOTSTRAP`,
  and asserts the resulting decision is `Decision.Deny` with `Decision.REASON_NO_GRANT` (the same

### 2026-09-06: `P4-T3` final slice implemented: Fields binding/occurrence operations mapped onto the Requirement resource

- Current phase and task: Phase 4, Authorization and Dual Access Surfaces. `P4-T3` is now complete
  apart from the correction-allowlist slice, which stays resolved as blocked on `P8-T3`. Phase 4 as a
  whole is complete through `P4-T3`; `P4-T4` is next and unstarted.
- Status at session end: Implemented the one remaining open slice of `P4-T3`, confirmed by auditing
  `InformationRequestFieldResourceAdapter.kt` and `InformationRequestFieldBindingPolicy.kt` per the
  prior session's handoff: `InformationRequestFieldBindingPolicy` was a placeholder
  (`isExternalCaller` always `false`, no per-binding rule at all) explicitly documented as "Temporary
  ... until party-scoped Requirement facts are available." Those facts have existed since `P3-T8`.
  Traced how one Field binding maps to one Requirement:
  `InformationRequestTemplateRequirementBinding.collectedFieldDefinitionId` names the stable Field
  Definition a FIELD-type Requirement answers, and `SchemaFieldBinding.fieldDefinitionId` names the
  same stable identity for a binding of the request's assigned Schema, so matching the two identifies
  the Requirement one binding answers. Rewrote `InformationRequestFieldBindingPolicy.decide()` to,
  after the shared audience/read-only rule from `AudienceFieldBindingPolicy` passes, resolve that
  Requirement (via `InformationRequestRequirementRepository.findForRequest` joined in memory against
  `InformationRequestTemplateRequirementBindingRepository.findById`) and ask the central
  `AuthorizationService` for `INFORMATION_REQUEST_REQUIREMENT_VIEW` (read) or
  `INFORMATION_REQUEST_REQUIREMENT_RESPOND` (write) against
  `ResourceRef.informationRequestRequirement(requirementId)`, denying as `OUT_OF_AUDIENCE` on a central
  deny. A binding that answers no Requirement (a question the request itself asks) finds no match and
  is left to the shared audience rule, unchanged. `InformationRequestFieldResourceAdapter.authorizeViewFields`/
  `authorizeManageFields` were deliberately left authorizing the whole request: they are the coarse
  "may this principal touch Fields on this resource at all" gate the binding policy's finer per-question
  filter runs inside of, not a duplicate of it.
- Tests added first: New file `InformationRequestFieldBindingPolicyTest.kt` with four cases: (1) a
  binding answering a Requirement is denied when central authorization denies
  `INFORMATION_REQUEST_REQUIREMENT_RESPOND` for that Requirement; (2) the same is permitted once
  central authorization allows `INFORMATION_REQUEST_REQUIREMENT_VIEW`; (3) a binding answering no
  Requirement is allowed without consulting `AuthorizationService` at all; (4) a read-only binding is
  still denied for writes by the shared base rule without consulting the Requirement repository or
  `AuthorizationService`.
- Failure observed before implementation: Compilation failure, not a runtime assertion failure --
  `InformationRequestFieldBindingPolicy(requirementRepository = ..., templateBindingRepository = ...,
  authorizationService = ...)` did not resolve because the class still had its no-arg constructor
  (`No parameter with name 'requirementRepository' found`, and the same for the other two
  parameters), confirming the test exercised behavior that did not exist yet.
- Implementation completed: `InformationRequestFieldBindingPolicy` now takes
  `InformationRequestRequirementRepository`, `InformationRequestTemplateRequirementBindingRepository`,
  and `AuthorizationService` and implements the Requirement-occurrence mapping described above.
- Files changed:
  `src/main/kotlin/com/docuhyphen/app/api/service/informationrequest/InformationRequestFieldBindingPolicy.kt`
  (rewritten); new
  `src/test/kotlin/com/docuhyphen/app/api/service/informationrequest/InformationRequestFieldBindingPolicyTest.kt`;
  `src/test/kotlin/com/docuhyphen/app/api/service/informationrequest/InformationRequestFieldResourceAdapterTest.kt`

### 2026-09-06: `P4-T3` request-state slice: response mutations gated by an explicit request-state fact

- Current phase and task: Phase 4, Authorization and Dual Access Surfaces. `P4-T3` is in progress; the
  Exchange-ownership and request-state slices are complete, two slices remain (correction allowlist
  investigation and the Fields binding/occurrence mapping -- see "Exact next task" in `## Status`).
- Status at session end: Investigated the first open `P4-T3` slice from the prior session's handoff:
  "Request state is only consulted internally to derive `correctionScope`... confirm whether any
  decision actually needs the raw state before adding it, rather than adding an unused fact." Reading
  `InformationRequestRequirementPolicyEvaluator.kt` and `InformationRequestTransitionMatrix.kt` found a
  real gap, not an already-covered case: `answerMutationActions` (`RESPOND`/`ATTEST`/`EVIDENCE_UPLOAD`/
  `EVIDENCE_WITHDRAW`) were denied only by `responseMode` and `correctionScope`. `correctionScope` is
  `OPEN_CORRECTION` only when `request.state == CHANGES_REQUESTED`; every other non-terminal state
  (including `SUBMITTED` and `UNDER_REVIEW`, where a response has already been submitted for review)
  resolved to `NORMAL_RESPONSE`, so the evaluator would incorrectly `Permit` a response mutation while a
  request was submitted awaiting review or already under review. This diverges from
  `InformationRequestTransitionMatrix.ACTIVE_RESPONSE_STATES` (`ISSUED`/`IN_PROGRESS`/
  `CHANGES_REQUESTED`), the same set `InformationRequestFieldResourceAdapter.valuesEditable` already
  uses to gate Field value edits, so this brings the Requirement resource-policy evaluator's own
  mutation actions in line with a state boundary already enforced elsewhere in the codebase. Confirmed
  `isArchived` (terminal states: `CLOSED`/`CANCELLED`/`SUPERSEDED`/`EXPIRED`) already denies generically
  through `DefaultAuthorizationService`, so the fix only needed to cover the non-terminal
  `SUBMITTED`/`UNDER_REVIEW` gap, not terminal states.
- Tests added first: four cases added to `InformationRequestRequirementPolicyEvaluatorTest.kt` -- a
  `requestState` parameter (default `ISSUED`) added to the local `facts()` builder so every existing
  test keeps its prior meaning unchanged; `response mutation is denied while the request is submitted
  awaiting review` (`SUBMITTED`); `response mutation is denied while the request is under review`
  (`UNDER_REVIEW`); `viewing a Requirement is not blocked by request state` (confirms the new check is
  scoped to `answerMutationActions` only, not view/disclosure actions).
- Failure observed before implementation: Added the `requestState` field to
  `InformationRequestRequirementPolicyFacts` and wired it from the context provider first (structural,
  not decision logic, so it could not be red for the wrong reason), then ran the suite with the actual
  new evaluator check replaced by a no-op comment. `./mvnw -o test
  -Dtest=InformationRequestRequirementPolicyEvaluatorTest` failed exactly the two new deny-expecting

  the intended reason; the view-action test and all ten pre-existing tests passed unchanged, confirming
  the gap was isolated to the two new mutation-during-submitted/under-review cases before any narrowing
  logic existed.
- Implementation completed: `InformationRequestRequirementPolicyFacts.kt` gained a new required

  gap, unlike the `P4-T1`/`P4-T2` sessions which found their scope already implemented uncommitted.
  `RoleCapabilities.forExchangeShareRole(OWNER)` already carries
  `INFORMATION_REQUEST_CREATE`/`READ`/`CANCEL`/`ADMIN` (added by `P3-T13`), but that grant lives on a
  Share row scoped to the Exchange resource (`resourceType = EXCHANGE`). `ParentGrantInheritanceResolver.evaluate`
  only admits inheritance for a child `ResourceKind` that has a registered `ParentGrantInheritancePolicy`
  (rule 1 in its own doc comment); before this session only
  `InformationRequestRequirementParentGrantInheritancePolicy` existed, registered for
  `ResourceKind.INFORMATION_REQUEST_REQUIREMENT`, and no policy was registered for
  `ResourceKind.INFORMATION_REQUEST` itself. Reading `InformationRequestLifecycleService.kt` (lines
  157, 192, 279-286) confirmed `cancel`/`supersede` authorize against
  `ResourceRef.informationRequest(requestId)` directly, not against the Exchange, so the owner's
  Exchange-scoped grant had no path to reach those decisions. Only request creation
  (`InformationRequestAdHocCreationService`) and the exchange-scoped list endpoint
  (`InformationRequestQueryService.listForExchange`), which both authorize against
  `ResourceRef.exchange(exchangeId)` directly, were ever reachable by the owner grant before this
  change.

    `InformationRequestParentGrantInheritancePolicy`, a mocked `ResourceAuthorizationContextRegistry`
    resolving the request's context with `parentRef = ResourceRef.exchange(exchangeId)` and a matching

    `authorize(principal, Action.INFORMATION_REQUEST_CANCEL, ResourceRef.informationRequest(requestId), context)`
    is allowed, that `grantsOn` reports the grant's `inheritedFrom` as the Exchange ref, and that the
    inherited capability set contains `INFORMATION_REQUEST_CANCEL` but excludes
    `Capability.EXCHANGE_DELETE` and `Capability.DOCUMENT_WRITE` (both present on the same Exchange
    Share's full capability set).
  - "an unrelated principal is still denied" -- the same wiring with the Share issued to a different
    principal denies with `Decision.REASON_NO_GRANT`.

  `InformationRequestParentGrantInheritancePolicy` was first added as a bare pass-through implementing

### 2026-09-06: `P4-T1` `InformationRequestAccessContextFactory` no-auth bootstrap-session input path added

- Current phase and task: Phase 4, Authorization and Dual Access Surfaces. `P4-T1` is complete. The
  next unblocked task is `P4-T2`.
- Status at session end: Extended `InformationRequestAccessContextFactory` with its second explicit
  input path. The factory now offers `fromBootstrapSession(shareLink, session, participant)` alongside
  the existing `currentAuthenticated()`, both returning the same `RequestAccessContext` shape.
  `RequestAccessSession` does not yet exist as a persisted entity anywhere in the repository (`P4-T4`
  adds that persistence), so this task introduces it as a plain, non-persisted data class carrying
  only what the factory needs today: `id`, `shareLinkId`, `expiresAt`, `revokedAt`. It deliberately
  does not carry the resolved participant principal, a raw credential, or a secret; resolving the
  participant `PrincipalRef` that a session is bound to, and validating recipient contact proof, both
  remain the job of the no-auth surface `P4-T5` adds, not of this factory or this shape. `P4-T4` is
  expected to grow this shape into the full persisted `RequestAccessSession` entity Architectural
  Decision 24 and Decision 36 describe (authentication strength, request-party binding, atomic use
  tracking, lineage), not replace it with an unrelated type.
- Tests added first: Extended `InformationRequestAccessContextFactoryTest` with four cases: a
  validated bootstrap session becomes a request access context carrying the resolved participant (and
  the session's own id as `AuthorizationContext.sessionRef`, never the ShareLink token or any secret);
  a session bound to a different ShareLink is refused; a revoked session is refused; an expired
  session is refused.
- Failure observed before implementation: Compile-red -- `mvn test -Dtest=InformationRequestAccessContextFactoryTest`
  failed with eight `Unresolved reference` errors (`RequestAccessSession`, `fromBootstrapSession`) at
  test-compile, confirming the intended missing-production-code failure rather than a runtime
  assertion failure.
- Implementation completed: Added `RequestAccessSession.kt` (plain data class, not a JPA entity) in
  `service/informationrequest`. Extended `InformationRequestAccessContextFactory` with
  `fromBootstrapSession(shareLink: ShareLink, session: RequestAccessSession, participant: PrincipalRef): RequestAccessContext`,
  which throws `ForbiddenException` when `session.shareLinkId != shareLink.id` (defends against a
  caller wiring together an inconsistent credential/session pair), when `session.revokedAt != null`,
  or when `session.expiresAt` is in the past (computed against `Instant.now()` at call time, matching
  the `P3-T12` precedent of computing "now" internally rather than accepting an `asOf` parameter).
  On success it builds `AuthorizationContext(sessionRef = session.id.toString())` -- the session's own
  non-secret id, never `shareLinkTokenHash`, keeping a bootstrap-mode ShareLink from ever reading as a
  `PUBLIC_LINK` content grant through this path, consistent with Architectural Decision 24.
- Files changed:
  - `src/main/kotlin/com/docuhyphen/app/api/service/informationrequest/RequestAccessSession.kt` (new)
  - `src/main/kotlin/com/docuhyphen/app/api/service/informationrequest/InformationRequestAccessContextFactory.kt`
  - `src/test/kotlin/com/docuhyphen/app/api/service/informationrequest/InformationRequestAccessContextFactoryTest.kt`
- Database migrations added: None. `RequestAccessSession` is not persisted by this task.
- Focused tests run and results: `./mvnw -o test -Dtest=InformationRequestAccessContextFactoryTest`
  passes, 7 tests, 0 failures (grew from 3 to 7 cases).
- Full validation commands and results: `./mvnw -o test -Dtest="com.docuhyphen.app.api.**.informationrequest.**"`
  reports Tests run: 206, Failures: 0, Errors: 4, Skipped: 16. The 4 errors are the same pre-existing
  Docker/Kafka-dependent `@QuarkusTest` failures already journaled in the `P3-T12` and `P3-T13`
  entries (`InformationRequestTemplatePersistenceContractTest`,
  `InformationRequestTemplateConfigurationWriterContractTest`,
  `InformationRequestTemplatePublicationContractTest`,
  `InformationRequestTemplateWalkingSkeletonContractTest`, all failing on
  `DevServicesKafkaProcessor` because no local Docker daemon is available in this session's sandbox),

- Help documentation reviewed or updated: Searched help docs for "information request" (case
  insensitive); only `fieldsSection.tsx` and `informationRequestTemplatesArticle.tsx` matched, both

- Decisions made: Kept `RequestAccessSession` a plain data class rather than a JPA `@Entity` or a

  run because no file under `web-app/` was touched this session.
- Decisions made:
  1. The Exchange owner is a deliberate, narrow, documented exception to default-deny for exactly
     four runtime request capabilities (`CREATE`, `READ`, `CANCEL`, `ADMIN`), because no request-
     scoped Share can exist before the request itself does. This is the "resource-scoped role grant"
     `InformationRequestAuthorizationVocabularyTest`'s prior comment anticipated
     ("default-deny until a resource-scoped role grant is added"), not a reversal of the default-deny
     principle: every other role, and every other runtime capability on the owner's own grant, stays
     untouched and still requires a request-scoped Share.
  2. `INFORMATION_REQUEST_ADMIN` is the capability `Action.INFORMATION_REQUEST_SUPERSEDE`,
     `MANAGE_PARTIES`, and `REASSIGN_PARTY` all require; there is no finer-grained capability that
     covers supersession without also covering party management. Granting it to the owner therefore
     also permits the owner to reassign and manage request parties (`P3-T11a`'s `reassignMutation`)
     as a side effect. This was accepted rather than redesigning the existing capability granularity,
     since an owner administering their own request's parties is consistent with the "owner-only"
     framing of this task and no existing task scoped party management away from the owner.
  3. `InformationRequestEntitlementGuard` is a separate class from
     `InformationRequestTemplateEntitlementGuard` rather than a generalization of it, because a
     runtime request's owner is read directly from its parent `Exchange`, while a Template's owner is
     named by an explicit `scopeKind` the caller supplies. Forcing both through one shared shape
     would need the Template call sites to keep synthesizing an `Exchange`-shaped owner, or the
     Exchange call sites to keep synthesizing a `scopeKind`, for no shared behavior beyond the two
     `SubscriptionAccessService` calls each method already makes directly.
  4. `requestETag` is a field on `InformationRequestDto`, not a response header, because `list`
     returns several requests at once and a header can carry only one value; `create`/`cancel`/
     `supersede` each still also set the `ETag` response header (matching the existing
     `InformationRequestDelegatedAuthorityResource` convention) since those responses carry exactly
     one request.
  5. No REST endpoint for issuance, single-request `GET`, or party management was added. The task
     text names exactly list, draft creation, cancellation, and supersession; a pinned resource test
     (`no issuance or respondent action is exposed`) enforces the boundary.
- Assumptions: none beyond what the plan already states. The Exchange fixtures in
  `InformationRequestAdHocCreationServiceTest` and `InformationRequestLifecycleServiceTest` already
  set `ownerOrganizationId`, so the new entitlement-guard dependency in both fixtures is a plain
  mock with no stubbing required (a `Unit`-returning method no-ops by default).
- Known risks or blockers: None new. The `P3-T11b`/`c`/`d` blockers are unchanged. The three Docker-

    matcher/literal invocation. Reverted to the original 3-parameter signature and compute the

  transition row's `partyId`, `fromState`/`toState`, audit event type, and domain event) and
  `InformationRequestPartyServiceTest."reassigning a party rechecks the locked parent Exchange and denies when it is terminal"`
  (proves an `ENDED` parent Exchange denies reassignment before any Share or party mutation, and no

### 2026-09-04: `P3-T8` command-safe delegated-authority grant and revoke lifecycle implemented

- Current phase and task: Phase 3. `P3-T8` remains in progress and unchecked.
- Status at session end: Added `InformationRequestDelegatedAuthorityService` with `grant` and
  `revoke` commands over the existing minimal `information_request_delegated_authority` fact
  table. Both commands follow the same Command Receipt, `If-Match` precondition, and pessimistic
  row-lock shape as `InformationRequestPartyService`, and reuse the existing `partyRevision`
  list ETag rather than adding a new revision column, because a delegated authority only ever
  narrows or restores who may act for an already-existing assigned party. The full authority
  instrument, effective and expiry dates, and revocation history remain assigned to the later
  `P3-T12` delegated-authority model task; this slice only makes the existing minimal fact rows
  safely mutable end to end.
- Tests added first: Added `InformationRequestDelegatedAuthorityServiceTest` covering: granting
  authority for an active acting party advances `partyRevision` and records an active fact;
  granting without the current parties ETag throws `CommandPreconditionException`; granting for a
  revoked party, a subject party, an unsupported delegate principal kind (`PUBLIC_LINK`), or a
  Requirement belonging to a different request is refused before any row is saved; replaying a
  grant with the same idempotency key returns the stored authority without a second insert or a
  second `partyRevision` advance; revoking an active authority advances `partyRevision` and marks
  it inactive; revoking an already-revoked authority or one from a different request is refused.
  The first compile-capable red run failed with `IllegalArgumentException: Delegated authority
  receipt target not found` in the replay test only, because the test fixture stubbed
  `authorityRepository.findByIdForUpdate` but not `findById`, which the service's replay path

- Implementation completed: Added `InformationRequestDelegatedAuthorityService.kt` with
  `GrantInformationRequestDelegatedAuthorityCommand` and
  `RevokeInformationRequestDelegatedAuthorityCommand`. Grant validates the assigned party belongs
  to the request, is active, and is not the subject role; validates the delegate principal kind
  against the same allowed set as the `ck_information_request_delegated_authority_principal`
  database check (`USER`, `PARTICIPANT`, `PRINCIPAL_GROUP`); and validates an optional Requirement
  scope belongs to the same request before the database trigger would refuse it. Revoke validates
  the authority belongs to the request and is still active. Both authorize through the existing
  `Action.INFORMATION_REQUEST_MANAGE_PARTIES` action, reusing the party-administration capability
  rather than adding a new Action, because granting or revoking who may act for an existing party
  is the same administrative surface as assigning or revoking the party itself. Added
  `ResourceType.INFORMATION_REQUEST_DELEGATED_AUTHORITY` as a command-result-only marker type,
  mirroring `INFORMATION_REQUEST_PARTY`; it carries no Share rows and needed no Share migration.

  exhaustive `when` over `ResourceType` that required a new arm.

### 2026-09-02: `P3-T1e` parent-grant inheritance and resource policy evaluator implemented

- Current phase and task: Phase 3. `P3-T1e` is complete and `P3-T1f` is next.
- Status at session end: The central authorization stack now has two registered-only extension
  contracts. A resource kind takes the grants held on its parent only when a
  `ParentGrantInheritancePolicy` is registered for that kind, and only for exactly one level whose
  parent resolves its own facts and shares the child's owner. Self references and mutual references
  are refused as cycles, an unresolvable or context-free parent refuses the decision, and an owner
  mismatch refuses it. A `ResourcePolicyEvaluator` may narrow an already-allowed decision with facts
  only its kind understands, but can never widen one. Nothing registers either contract yet, so no
  decision made today changes.
- Tests added first:
  - `src/test/kotlin/com/docuhyphen/app/api/service/auth/authz/ParentGrantInheritanceTest.kt`:
    proves inheritance is off until registered, that a registered kind reaches exactly its parent's
    grants, that the grandparent is never reached, that owner mismatch, self reference, mutual
    reference, and an unresolvable parent each refuse by their own reason, and that an inherited
    Share grant still answers to that Share's own constraints.
  - `src/test/kotlin/com/docuhyphen/app/api/service/auth/authz/ResourcePolicyEvaluatorTest.kt`:
    proves an unregistered kind is unchanged, a registered evaluator can deny or attach obligations,
    unavailable facts fail closed, the evaluator sees the resolved capabilities, and it is never
    asked about a decision the central capability union already refused.
- Failure observed before implementation:
  - `.\mvnw.cmd -o test "-Dtest=ParentGrantInheritanceTest,ResourcePolicyEvaluatorTest"`: 14 run,
    8 failures, 2 errors. Every refusal returned `NO_GRANT` because no parent was consulted, the
    inherited-capability case was denied, and both evaluator denial cases returned `Allow`. The four
    default-off cases passed from the first run, which is the behavior they pin.
- Implementation completed:
  - Added `ParentGrantInheritancePolicy`, the `ParentGrantInheritance` answer type, the CDI policy
    registry, and `ParentGrantInheritanceResolver` holding the one-level, owner-matched, cycle-safe,
    fail-closed rules.
  - Added `ResourcePolicyEvaluator`, its request and outcome types, and the CDI evaluator registry.
  - Added `Decision` reasons `PARENT_CONTEXT_UNRESOLVED`, `PARENT_OWNER_MISMATCH`,
    `PARENT_INHERITANCE_CYCLE`, and `RESOURCE_POLICY_FACTS_UNAVAILABLE`.
  - Added `Grant.inheritedFrom` so an inherited grant records the resource it came from while
    keeping its own source kind and identity, which leaves every share constraint, expiry, and
    obligation rule applying to it unchanged.
  - Wired both contracts into `DefaultAuthorizationService`: inheritance is answered once per
    decision and passed into grant collection, and the evaluator runs after the capability union and
    the archived and suspended denies, merging its obligations most-restrictively.
  - Added `ResourceAuthorizationContextRegistry.kindOf` so the resolver asks one place which kind a
    reference is.

- Decisions made:
  - An inherited grant keeps its own `Grant.SourceKind` and `sourceId` rather than being retagged.
    Retagging would have taken an inherited Share grant out of the share-constraint path and made it
    count as independently capable, which would have skipped MFA, IP, expiry, and status checks.
    `inheritedFrom` records the provenance instead.
  - A refused inheritance refuses the whole decision rather than silently falling back to the
    child's own grants, so a parent reference that cannot be proved safe never degrades quietly.
  - An evaluator may only deny or attach obligations. Allowing one to grant would have created a
    second allowance path beside the central capability union.
  - The two registries are constructor parameters with empty defaults, so the released behavior of
    every existing caller and test is unchanged while CDI still injects the real registries.
- Assumptions: no resource kind registers either contract yet, so today's decisions are unchanged.
  `P3-T8` registers the Requirement-occurrence inheritance policy and the request policy evaluator
  once the runtime entities and their providers exist.

### 2026-09-02: `P3-T1b` unresolved-resource-context correction implemented

- Current phase and task: Phase 3. `P3-T1b` is complete and `P3-T1c` is next.
- Status at session end: The central authorization stack now fails closed for every resource type
  that states it carries its own authorization facts. Such a resource is refused with
  `RESOURCE_CONTEXT_UNRESOLVED` when those facts cannot be produced, contributes no grants at all,
  and no longer borrows organization roles from the caller's selected organization. The platform
  control-plane types, which state that they carry no resource context, keep their previous
  behavior including the active-organization path. A Principal Group now states its own owner
  through its own provider, so group management keeps working on the group's ownership rather than
  on an unresolved fallback.
- Tests added first:
  - `src/test/kotlin/.../service/auth/authz/UnresolvedResourceContextPolicyTest.kt`, 9 tests: the
    three resolution outcomes, a governed resource whose row is gone, the deny for a governed kind
    with no provider, the deny for a governed resource that cannot be located, the absence of grants
    for both, organization grants coming from the resolved owner, a personal owner yielding no
    organization grants, the retained active-organization path for the two control-plane types, and
    a group still resolving its owning organization.
  - `src/test/kotlin/.../service/organization/PrincipalGroupAuthorizationContextProviderTest.kt`,
    5 tests over an organization-owned group, a personal group, a co-owned group with no single
    owner, an unknown group, and the served kind.
- Failure observed before implementation: the resolution vocabulary and the group provider had to
  exist for the test source to compile, so they were added first with no change to
  `DefaultAuthorizationService`, and the behavioral red was taken on the decision path.
  `.\mvnw.cmd -o test "-Dtest=UnresolvedResourceContextPolicyTest,PrincipalGroupAuthorizationContextProviderTest"`
  reported 14 run, 3 failures, 0 errors: a governed kind with no provider was denied with
  `NO_GRANT` rather than the unresolved reason, the same for a governed resource whose row was
  gone, and such a resource still contributed grants.
- Implementation completed:
  - Added `ResourceContextResolution` with `Resolved`, `Unresolved`, and `NotGoverned`, and
    `ResourceAuthorizationContextRegistry.resolution`, which answers all three in one place. A type
    that maps to a `ResourceKind` states that it carries its own facts; a type that maps to none
    states that it carries no resource context.
  - Removed `requiresUnavailableProvider` and its provider-required set. The rule is no longer
    limited to the two request kinds: every governed kind is now decided from its own facts, which
    is what `P3-T1a` deliberately deferred to this task.
  - `DefaultAuthorizationService.authorize` resolves once, refuses an `Unresolved` resource before
    collecting anything, passes the same answer to grant collection, and reads the archived and
    suspended state from it rather than resolving a second time. `grantsOn` returns nothing for an
    `Unresolved` resource, and `collectOrgMembershipGrants` reads the owner from the resolved
    context, keeps the Principal Group branch, and uses `activeOrgId` only for a `NotGoverned` type.
  - Added `PrincipalGroupAuthorizationContextProvider` so the Principal Group kind, previously
    mapped with no provider, resolves its own owner.

  recorded as unconfirmed.
- Frontend validation: not run and not required. No file under `web-app` changed.
- Help documentation reviewed or updated: not required. No endpoint, label, navigation path,
  permission a user can hold, or lifecycle rule changed. The correction is internal to how an
  authorization decision resolves the resource it is about.
- Decisions made:
  - A mapped `ResourceKind` is the statement that a resource carries its own authorization facts,
    so the fail-closed rule keys off the mapping rather than a separate list. `APPLICATION` and
    `WORKFLOW_WEBHOOK_ENDPOINT` map to no kind deliberately and are the only place the
    active-organization path survives; audit governance, application management, and webhook
    endpoint management all decide on those references and are unchanged.
  - `DOCUMENT` is a governed kind with no provider, so it is now refused. No production code
    authorizes a Document reference: the only `ResourceType.DOCUMENT` uses in `src/main` are audit
    target labels. The refusal is therefore a correctness statement rather than a behavior change a
    user can reach, and it stays true until a Document provider exists.
  - `PRINCIPAL_GROUP` is a governed kind that two production paths do authorize, so this task gives
    it a provider rather than leaving group management refused. A co-owned group names no single
    owner in its own row and resolves to nothing, which refuses it; nothing in the codebase creates
    such a group, and giving one a fabricated single owner would be worse than refusing it.
  - Group deactivation is not reported as archival. Reporting it would change who may act on an
    inactive group, which is a separate decision from resolving its owner.
  - The probe default in the shared Exchange permutation fixture means "this test says nothing about
    resource state", not "this Exchange cannot be resolved", so it now resolves to an
    organization-owned Exchange whose owner the caller is not a member of. Shares alone still decide
    those permutations.
- Assumptions: the registry mock in a unit test now has to state its outcome, which is why five
  existing test classes changed; none of their assertions were weakened, and the two that
  previously stubbed an unresolvable Exchange now state an owner instead. The one test that already
  asserted no organization grants for an unresolvable Exchange kept its assertion and now passes for
  the intended reason rather than by omission.
- Industry-neutrality audit: every added identifier names a generic authorization concept, being
  resolution, resolved, unresolved, not governed, owner, and group. The new provider is named for
  the existing neutral `PrincipalGroup` entity. No industry vocabulary, customer name, seeded
  configuration, or shipped default appears, and no production branch reads a customer-authored key.
- Known risks or blockers: none blocking `P3-T1c`. Two carried items remain. First,
  `share_resource_type_check` still admits only `EXCHANGE`, `DOCUMENT`, and `PRINCIPAL_GROUP`, so
  `P3-T1c` must widen it before `P3-T8` inserts a request-party Share. Second, the request kinds
  remain unreachable by design until `P3-T8` registers their providers; that is now the same
  mechanism every other governed kind uses rather than a special case.
- Exact next task: `P3-T1c`. Generalize `Share.roleName` from `ExchangeShareRoleName` to a
  resource-scoped role key with a resource-kind capability registry, through an expand-contract
  migration that widens `share_resource_type_check` and `share_role_name_check`, preserves every
  existing Share row, and replaces both Exchange-only database checks with resource-aware

- Decisions made:
  - The Requirement occurrence is a resource type of its own rather than a field on the aggregate,
    because assignment, response mode, confidentiality, and correction scope are decided per
    occurrence and the central stack addresses decisions by resource.
  - Fail-closed is scoped here to the two kinds this task introduces rather than applied to every
    mapped kind. Making the generic path fail closed changes existing behavior for `DOCUMENT`,
    `APPLICATION`, and `WORKFLOW_WEBHOOK_ENDPOINT`, which has to be characterized first; that is
    `P3-T1b`. The provider-required set is the seam between the two.
  - `grantsOn` returns nothing for a provider-required resource rather than relying on the action
    check to deny. Otherwise `capabilities()` would report organization capabilities on a request
    resource even though `authorize` refused it, and a caller reading capabilities to build a UI
    would be told it may act.
  - Requirement view reuses `INFORMATION_REQUEST_READ` rather than adding a second read capability.
    The resource type is carried by the `ResourceRef`, which is how the existing model separates
    document reads from Exchange reads.
  - Submission is an action on the request rather than on one occurrence, because a package covers
    the occurrences of one request.
- Assumptions: the registry's exhaustive `when` over `ResourceType` was the only site that adding an
  enum value could break, verified by searching every `ResourceType.` and `ResourceKind.` branch in
  `src/main`. `Share.roleName` remains Exchange-typed, so nothing in this task can write a request
  Share even by accident.

  and actions speak of requests, requirements, responses, attestations, review, evidence, and
  export; the refusal codes name entitlement, rollout, lifecycle, precondition, and assignment

  - The three rules are asked at three different points on purpose. Whether a typed requirement names
    a field is a fact about one row, so the write settles it and an author is told immediately.
    Whether one Version names a field twice is a fact about the Version, so the index settles it.
    Whether the Version's contract carries the field spans two statements that reach storage
    separately during one whole-document rewrite, so asking at write time would refuse a coherent
    document for the order its parts arrived in.
  - The reference is to the stable Field Definition rather than to a Field Contract. A Schema Version
    binds a contract version, and two Schema Versions may bind different contract versions of one
    field; the definition is the thing that stays the same across both and across a later Template
    Version asking the same requirement again.
  - The write guard reads the requirement type through `NEW.template_requirement_id` rather than
    through the existing `request_template_binding_requirement_type` helper, which looks a binding up
    by its own id and therefore finds nothing during a `BEFORE INSERT`.
  - An empty permitted-answer set now means the plain provided answer and nothing else. The stored
    waiver rule already reads the set as an allowlist, so an empty set cannot simultaneously mean
    that everything is permitted; the reading is stored rather than left implicit, which also lets
    the `REQUIRED_ON_EXCEPTION` rule stop exempting an empty set. A party that cannot answer is
    offered nothing, so its set stays empty.

    have produced. Its copy test compares a Version inserted directly against one written through
    the validator, and without that the settlement would have shown up as a false disagreement
    between the two.

  is a second, additional way of naming a Schema Version and no existing path calls it.
- Decisions made:
  - The owner question is asked while a draft is authored, not only when it freezes. Publication is
    the last point at which a missing answer can be supplied, but an author choosing a Version they
    may not use should be told immediately, while choosing another one is still cheap.
  - The check is asked about the owner stored on the Template rather than the caller's selected
    organization, matching every other decision in this service. This is what makes a clone into
    another owner refuse: cloning routes through `replaceDraftConfiguration` on the new Template.
  - Starting a new Version from a published one deliberately does not recheck the Schema. The source
    configuration was already validated and its owner has not changed, and rechecking would let a
    later Schema retirement block an author from continuing a Template that already exists.
  - The refusal is a Fields exception translated into a Template exception rather than allowed to
    escape. A Fields refusal leaving the Template authoring surface would map to whatever the Fields
    resources map it to, which is a different contract from the one the Template resource states.
  - The resolver lives in the Fields domain and owns the two Fields repositories it reads, rather
    than the Template service reading them. That keeps the Template domain talking to Fields through
    a method, and keeps the exact-Version question next to the assign-latest question it must not be
    confused with.
  - A never-disclosed requirement remains legal when it is optional and states no permitted answers.
    The requesting side may track something the responding party never sees; what is refused is only
    the combination that asks that party for something.
  - The `REQUIRED_ON_EXCEPTION` rule fires only on a non-empty permitted set. An empty set is
    currently ambiguous: the stored waiver rule reads the set as an allowlist, while nothing refuses
    an empty one, which would mean a requirement that permits no answer at all. Rather than guess,
    the rule is written so it cannot depend on the answer, and settling the meaning is recorded in
    `P2-T10b`.
  - Contradictory single-row bounds are still not restated in Kotlin. V88 refuses each of them as a
    stored constraint, and a second copy would drift.
- Assumptions: `InformationRequestTemplateAuthoringService.replaceDraftConfiguration` is the only
  path that writes a `schema_version_id` onto a draft, verified by grep for `schemaVersionId =` in

  copying an already-validated document.

- Decisions made:
  - A Blueprint names a Version, not a Template. Naming a Template would mean the request created
    tomorrow could resolve different configuration from the one created today, which is the exact
    property every request pinning its Version exists to prevent.
  - Selecting and instantiating are separate service questions with separate refusals. One is a
    choice made once from what is publishable now; the other is asked on every instantiation,
    possibly long afterwards. Collapsing them would either block editing a Blueprint whose Version
    was retired or let a retired Version silently keep producing requests.
  - The stored reference survives retirement. Refusing to save an unrelated field because the named
    Version was retired would freeze every Blueprint that named it, and losing the name would erase
    what the Blueprint used to create. An update that says nothing about the Version therefore never
    revalidates it, which a test pins.
  - A Blueprint may only name a Version its own owner holds, and a platform Blueprint may name none.
    Reusable request configuration belongs to an owner, and the platform holds neither the commercial
    entitlement nor the release grant that the resulting request would have to answer to.
  - A copy for a different owner starts without a name rather than refusing the copy or carrying the
    name across. Carrying it would produce a Blueprint whose every instantiation was refused;
    refusing the copy would let a Version reference block an ordinary duplicate. The dropped name is
    visible in the response rather than silent.
  - Removal is stated separately from selection. `UpdateBlueprintRequest` already treats a null
    `schemaDefinitionId` as unchanged unless `fieldDefaults` is supplied, and reusing that coupling
    for the Version would have made clearing it impossible; naming and clearing in one update is
    refused rather than resolved by precedence.
  - The foreign key restricts rather than nulling. A published Version cannot be deleted anyway, but
    forgetting a reference silently would change what a Blueprint creates without anybody deciding
    to.
  - The refusal extends `IllegalArgumentException` so the existing Blueprint resource maps it to
    `400` with its message and no resource change was needed. The machine-readable error body
    belongs with the stable error catalog in `P3-T1`.
  - `BlueprintTenantBoundaryTest`'s blueprint builder assigns
    `this.organizationId = if (scope == ORG) organizationId else null` inside an `apply`, where the
    right-hand name resolves to the entity's own null property rather than the test's organization.
    The new test hit the same trap and now holds the value in a local first. The pre-existing
    occurrence was left alone because no assertion there depends on it; it is recorded here as a
    latent fixture defect.

### 2026-09-01: `P2-T7c` implemented, `P2-T7` complete

- Current phase and task: Phase 2. `P2-T7c` and its parent `P2-T7` are complete; `P2-T8` is next.
- Status at session end: An authorized Template owner can retire a published Version, create one new
  editable Version from an explicitly selected published source, and clone an explicitly selected
  published Version into a new Definition and draft owned by the caller's requested scope. Every
  copy writes fresh configuration rows through the established whole-document writer. Recorded
  capability rows are not part of that document and remain absent until the existing publication
  service derives them again. A Definition lock serializes competing new-Version attempts before
  either checks for a draft or allocates the next number. Clone takes the same lock on the source
  after read authorization so retirement cannot race the source-state decision. Retirement preserves
  every frozen configuration row and records the actor and time; retiring the only published Version
  retires a Definition only when it has no editable Version.

- Current phase and task: Phase 2. `P2-T7b` is complete; `P2-T7c` is next.

  Publication locks the draft, asks `request_template_required_capabilities` for the set implied by
  the stored configuration, records each capability at the contract version declared by
  `InformationRequestCapability`, flushes those rows, and changes the Version and Definition to
  `PUBLISHED` in the same transaction. The V89 publication trigger therefore compares the recorded
  and derived sets before the configuration freezes. A Version that configures no Requirement is
  refused before any row changes. Configuration replacement now takes the same draft row lock, so a
  save cannot race publication through a stale `DRAFT` observation. A classified publish audit event
  files under the Template owner, and the audit catalog version is 17.

  proving that publication records every derived capability at its current contract version before
  freezing, refuses an empty draft, requires an editable Version, and reuses the owner mutation and
  audit contracts. The production service existed initially with its real signature and a deliberate
  not-implemented refusal so the test compiled before its behavioral red state.
  `InformationRequestTemplatePublicationContractTest`, two PostgreSQL contract tests proving that a
  draft is transitioned through the real V89 derivation and freeze functions and that a typed-data
  completeness refusal rolls the recorded capability rows plus both statuses back together.
